If that doesn't work, I'll find out if I can move the hospital appointment to the afternoon and contact you again. Rather than forcing it to match unreasonably, determining it clearly in advance seems better for both of us. I'll let you know again sometime today.
B2:팀장님, 상황을 알려 주셔서 감사합니다. 다만 이번 주말은 이미 가: Team leader, thank you for letting me know the situation. However, this weekend already has a family trip booked, so I can only find it difficult to attend. If I had known in advance, adjustment would have been possible, but it is a pity because it is a sudden request. Instead, I will finish the part I am in charge of as much as possible by Friday evening. If urgent confirmation is needed over the weekend, I can help even through a phone call, so please contact me comfortably. Next time, if you ask about the schedule in advance, I think I can cooperate more flexibly. Thank you for your understanding.
B2:문의해 주셔서 감사합니다, 설명이 부족했던 것 같아 죄송합니다. 처: Thank you for your inquiry, and I apologize that the explanation was insufficient. After the initial estimate, draft requests increased from three to five times, and in addition, final file format requests were additionally received, which further increased working time. Not only was there a request to move up the deadline, but the fact that the color palette had to be thoroughly re-examined was also reflected in the additional cost. I should have guided you on estimate changes each time, but not doing so is my mistake. I will organize the detailed work history by draft and send it again. If adjustment is needed regarding the amount, please feel free to tell me. From now on, whenever changes occur, I will guide you in advance.
Thank you for mentioning it, I was actually worried about the wall condition too. However, looking closely, the damage on that side seems much more severe compared to our side, so I am a bit worried whether a fifty-fifty split is correct. The damage caused by that tree falling during the past typhoon seems to have worked more heavily compared to our problem. Still, I don't want to flush faces between neighbors, so I want to propose getting an accurate estimate and dividing it reasonably compared to the damage ratio. How about getting estimates from two or three companies and discussing it again? I hope it gets resolved in a good direction.
B2:연락해 줘서 고마워, 얼마나 급하면 나한테 연락했을까 싶어서 마음이: Thanks for contacting me, I felt concerned thinking about how desperate you must have been to contact me. But to be honest, my situation lately has no spare either, so I am sorry that it will end up helping even a little bit. Rather than lending a large sum of money, it feels like it merely extends words of comfort, so my heart is heavy too. Instead, I think I can help with about 300,000 won for the urgent part, is that okay? It might end up being insufficient help with that, but I'll also look into other loan products or support systems together. Don't suffer alone and talk to me again whenever you need to.
B2:조용한 사직이란 회사를 실제로 그만두는 것이 아니라 정해진 업무 시: Quiet quitting refers to an attitude of not actually quitting the company but working only within designated working hours and scope. In other words, it is a declaration that you will follow only the minimum contract conditions and make no further dedication. This trend is not only a reaction against excessive overtime and burnout but also an attempt to re-establish the boundary between work and life. Spreading mainly among the younger generation, this phenomenon shows an attitude that values personal time more than promotion or recognition. From the company's perspective, there are voices concerned about decreased productivity, but from the worker's perspective, it is also accepted as an exercise of legitimate rights. Ultimately, quiet quitting can be said to be a symbolic phenomenon showing generational value differences regarding labor.
B2:한국의 회식 문화는 팀워크를 다지는 자리로 여겨지는 데 반해 서구: While Korea's hoesik culture is considered a place to build teamwork, in Western societies, hoesik is much rarer and often voluntary. In Korea, people tend to drink alcohol together at hoesik and build bonds, whereas in the West, privacy is valued and attendance is relatively free. These differences naturally stem from the difference between a culture that views an organization as a single community and a culture that focuses on the individual. Recently in Korea as well, complaints about mandatory hoesik culture are increasing, giving rise to alternatives like lunchtime hoesik or cultural hoesik. As generations change, perceptions of hoesik naturally change as well. Ultimately, hoesik culture can be said to show directly how each society views work and relationships.
B2:한국의 수능 준비는 보통 고등학교 삼 년 내내 이어지며 새벽부터 밤: Preparing for Korea's CSAT usually continues throughout all three years of high school, and because studies continue from early morning to late at night, students' daily patterns change entirely to focus on tests. As many students go back and forth between cram schools and reading rooms, they pour most of their day into studying. On the day of the test, an atmosphere is created where the whole society considers the test-takers, to the extent that even aircraft takeoff and landing times are adjusted. Parents even visit temples or churches to pray for their children, with the whole family spending the day in shared tension. As the test approaches, students' stress and anxiety often increase together. Because a single day of testing prepared this way largely determines the direction of university admissions, the CSAT holds symbolic meaning in Korean society.
B2:몇 년 전부터 스마트폰 애플리케이션을 통한 중고 거래가 크게 늘어났: Starting a few years ago, secondhand transactions through smartphone applications have increased significantly. As people frequently use platforms where they can easily buy and sell items, the size of the secondhand trading market naturally grew. This goes beyond a simple change in consumption patterns, reflecting a trend that values sharing over ownership. Since sellers dispose of unnecessary items to earn income and buyers can get items at low prices, a structure beneficial to both was formed. As the method of meeting and trading directly with neighborhood neighbors gained popularity, a new form of trust relationship was created within the local community. Ultimately, the growth of the secondhand market can be said to be an example that achieved both economic efficiency and environmental protection values together.
B2:한국어는 상대방의 나이와 사회적 지위에 따라 존댓말과 반말을 뚜렷하: While the Korean language clearly distinguishes between honorifics and non-honorifics according to the other person's age and social status, the Japanese language divides the degree of honorifics more minutely depending on the situation and relationship. In Korean, when meeting for the first time, people often check age and then decide whether to use honorifics, whereas in Japanese, social position or affiliation becomes a more important criterion than age. In both languages, honorifics not only express politeness but also play a role in adjusting the distance of the relationship. While it is common in Korea to switch to non-honorifics when becoming close, in Japan there are many relationships that maintain honorifics even after a long time. These differences show not only linguistic habits but also the difference in how the two societies view human relationships. Ultimately, the honorific system can be said to be a mirror that reflects the hierarchy and relationship culture of each society as it is.
B2:한국의 아파트 청약 제도는 신규 분양 아파트를 살 사람을 정하는 방: Korea's apartment subscription system is a method of determining who will buy newly offered apartments, giving priority by scoring periods of homelessness and the number of dependents. As long as you keep a subscription savings account for a certain period or more, you can get subscription eligibility, so many people make accounts in advance. When applying for subscriptions to popular complexes in certain regions, the competition rate can reach hundreds to one. Because you get more points for being homeless, it is evaluated as being designed to be advantageous to actual demanders. Conversely, if you win a subscription multiple times, there are regulations limiting re-winning for a certain period. Ultimately, this system was created with the purpose of fairly distributing limited housing, but it also generates debates between actual demanders and investors.
B2:스트리밍 서비스가 늘어날수록 시청자들은 정해진 시간에 텔레비전 앞에: As streaming services increase, viewers no longer need to sit in front of the television at set times and can watch desired content whenever they want. If traditional broadcasters merely insist on real-time scheduling, it has become difficult for them to keep up with rapidly changing viewer demands. As platforms diversify, production companies are pressured to invest more capital and create competitive original content. Not only did viewers' options widen, but the content production method and distribution structure itself were completely reorganized. As subscription fees rise, the burden on consumers using multiple services at the same time is also increasing. Ultimately, streaming services have not just changed the viewing method but have changed the landscape of the entire broadcasting industry.
B2:설날 아침이 되면 자녀들은 한복을 갖춰 입고 어른들께 새해 인사를: On the morning of Seollal, children wear traditional Hanbok and perform Sebae, offering New Year's greetings to the elders. Parents naturally teach children how to perform Sebae in advance so they have good manners. The elders who receive Sebae offer wise blessings and give New Year's money to the children, which contains the meaning of bringing good fortune in the new year. The younger they are, the greater their expectations for New Year's money, so children eagerly wait for Seollal. Recently, many families have come to put New Year's money in envelopes to deliver it sincerely. This custom can be said to be a representative holiday culture of Korea that allows generations to share politeness and affection.
B2:1인 가구 수가 꾸준히 늘어나는 이상 이들의 주거 수요를 충족시키는: As the number of single-person households steadily increases, the market satisfying their housing demand had no choice but to grow alongside it. Compared to existing large apartments, small housing units like studio apartments or officetels are popular because the burden of maintenance fees and rent is low. Since construction companies cannot ignore this demand, they are competitively supplying new units focused on small sizes. Compared to old small housing units, recent ones are evolving into forms with reinforced storage spaces and security facilities. As single-person households continue to increase, the growth trend of this market is projected to continue for the time being. Ultimately, the expansion of the small housing market can be said to be a phenomenon reflecting changing family types as they are.
B2:반려동물 등록제는 강아지를 키우는 보호자가 정부 시스템에 반려동물: The companion animal registration system is a system where guardians raising dogs must register their companion animal information in the government system. Since a fine can be imposed if caught without registration, most guardians try to comply with this. This system was introduced to reduce abandoned animal problems and increase the responsibility of guardians. There is also the advantage that if a companion animal goes missing, the owner can be found quickly through the registered information. The method of having animal hospitals insert an internal chip has settled as a representative registration procedure. Ultimately, this system can be said to be a social device allowing humans and animals to live safely together.
B2:한국의 비즈니스 자리에서는 처음 만난 사람과 명함을 주고받는 것이: In Korean business settings, exchanging business cards with someone you meet for the first time is considered basic etiquette. Business cards should be handed over and received politely with both hands, and it is considered polite to look at it for a moment rather than put it in your pocket immediately. In Western societies, business card exchange is relatively simple and formal, whereas in Korea, the process itself holds the meaning of confirming hierarchy and etiquette. A person of lower status hands over their business card first, and it must be delivered politely with both hands to a superior. Recently, while this formality has become somewhat simplified mainly among the younger generation, it is still strictly observed in traditional organizations. Ultimately, even a single business card etiquette contains the unique hierarchy and relationship culture of Korean society.
B2:재택근무가 보편화되면서 기업들은 고정된 개인 자리를 없애고 필요할: As telecommuting became common, companies began introducing methods to eliminate fixed personal seats and reserve seats only when needed. This change not only increases office space efficiency but also has the effect of reducing rental costs. Increasing shared spaces for collaboration instead of wide personal desks is essentially redefining the function of the office. Employees can move and work freely without fixed seats and can choose and work in spaces with their desired atmosphere. This change ultimately shows that the office has changed from a place to commute to every day into a hub for collaboration. Office spaces are expected to evolve into more flexible and diverse forms in the future.
B2:온라인 강의 플랫폼이 등장한 덕분에 학생들은 시간과 장소에 구애받지: Thanks to the appearance of online lecture platforms, students have become able to take desired lectures without being bound by time and place. As platforms diversified, opportunities to easily access lectures from famous universities around the world also increased. In the past, education was limited to taking place inside the classroom, but now repetitive learning tailored to individual speed has become possible. The fact that understanding increases the more you replay lecture videos is also an advantage unique to online lectures. Thanks to being able to receive quality education at a low cost, it also contributes to some extent to reducing the educational gap. Ultimately, online lectures can be said to be an innovative change that simultaneously enhances the accessibility and flexibility of education.
B2:SNS에서 새로운 카페나 팝업 스토어 사진이 빠르게 퍼지다 보니 사: As pictures of new cafes or pop-up stores spread quickly on SNS, a phenomenon of people flocking to them frequently appears. The more pictures are shared, the more special that place looks, so many people want to visit it themselves. Because they become a topic of conversation in a short time, these places easily go out of fashion quickly. Many people visit them even by pushing themselves because of the anxiety that they might be alienated from conversations if they don't follow trends. As consumer interests shift quickly, it is not easy for brands to maintain continuous freshness either. Ultimately, this trendy consumption culture can be said to be a phenomenon reflecting the thirst for newness and a sense of belonging at the same time.
B2:설날이나 추석 연휴가 되면 전국의 고속도로가 귀성 차량으로 가득 차: During Seollal or Chuseok holidays, highways nationwide fill with homecoming vehicles, so a distance that normally takes three hours can take over ten hours. Because many people move to their hometowns at the same time, severe congestion occurs on every road. Some sections experience severe congestion to the extent of crawling like a turtle at a few kilometers per hour. People find their own tricks, to the extent that an increasing number of people depart at dawn or late at night to avoid this situation. As congestion worsens, broadcasters continuously guide real-time traffic conditions. Ultimately, although holiday traffic congestion repeats every year, many people still willingly endure that time because it cannot break the heart to meet family.
B2:패스트 패션 브랜드는 유행에 맞춰 짧은 주기로 신제품을 출시하는 데: Fast fashion brands release new products in short cycles according to trends and choose mass-production methods to lower prices as much as possible. This method gives consumers the opportunity to buy the latest trendy clothes at low prices and inevitably results in encouraging fast consumption. There are criticisms that to lower production costs, clothes are made in countries with low labor costs and labor environment problems inevitably occur together. Because clothes are designed with short lifespans and the material quality is often low, they have no choice but to be discarded quickly. Clothes made this way ultimately lead to environmental pollution problems, and society has no choice but to shoulder disposal costs as well. Recently, reflecting on this structure, brands aiming for sustainable fashion are increasing.
B2:온라인 마켓의 당일 배송 시스템은 전국 곳곳에 위치한 물류 센터 덕: Online markets' same-day delivery system is designed so that products can be received within hours after ordering, thanks to logistics centers located all over the country. This system not only enhances consumer convenience but also has the effect of reducing the need for offline stores itself. Thanks to automated logistics systems, large volumes of orders can be processed in real-time. Delivery drivers not only efficiently tour assigned areas, but route optimization utilizing artificial intelligence is also carried out together. Thanks to the infrastructure enabling fast delivery, consumers gained immediate satisfaction. However, behind this convenience, tasks such as labor intensity and packaging waste problems remain.
B2:찜질방은 온탕과 사우나뿐만 아니라 식당, 수면실, 오락실까지 갖춘: Jjimjilbang is a Korea-unique complex relaxation space equipped with restaurants, sleeping rooms, and arcade rooms in addition to hot baths and saunas. It is equipped with various facilities so that you won't get bored even if you stay all day, making it natural for the whole family to enjoy together. Since you can use various facilities with a low admission fee, it is a cost-effective leisure space. During holidays or consecutive breaks, people looking for Jjimjilbangs open late naturally increase. As you spend time in one space with strangers, a culture of naturally sharing affection is formed. Ultimately, Jjimjilbang can be said to have established itself beyond a simple bath facility into a space for socialization and relaxation in the daily lives of Koreans.
B2:지하철 임산부 배려석은 객차마다 분홍색으로 표시되어 있어 승객들이: Subway pregnant-consideration seats are marked in pink in each carriage so that passengers can easily recognize them. This seat is a system prepared so that early pregnant women can use seats comfortably. By placing guide phrases and badges together on the seats, it induces citizens to naturally leave the seats empty. The intent of this system is to allow passengers wearing pregnant-woman badges to receive consideration even if they are not easily noticeable. Recently, some local governments are trying to raise citizen awareness through promotional campaigns. Ultimately, this system can be said to be operated in a way that relies on citizens' voluntary consideration rather than legal coercion.
B2:한국에서 살아가는 이상 종이, 플라스틱, 유리, 캔을 종류별로 나누: Living in Korea, separating and discharging paper, plastic, glass, and cans by type has settled as a basic living rule. Fines may be imposed if separation-discharge days or regulations are not followed. If recyclables are discharged in a contaminated state, they are often filtered out as they are during the recycling process and incinerated. Living together in an apartment complex, keeping designated discharge times and locations is considered important etiquette. Recently, when even a system that calculates food waste by weight and imposes fees is introduced, residents' cooperation becomes even more important. Ultimately, the separate-discharge system can be said to be a representative example where small individual practices gather to contribute to resource circulation.
B2:한국의 결혼식에서는 하객이 축하의 뜻으로 봉투에 현금을 담아 전달하: At Korean weddings, a congratulatory money culture where guests put cash in envelopes and deliver it as a sign of celebration has settled. The amount varies according to the degree of intimacy, and usually, closer relationships tend to pay larger amounts. Compared to wedding gift cultures in other countries, Korean congratulatory money is characterized by the fact that the amount circulates like a set standard. The bride and groom's sides organize the received congratulatory money and return the favor later, so it is also regarded as a means of continuing relationships. Compared to the past, recently the number of people delivering congratulatory money through mobile remittances is increasing. Ultimately, the congratulatory money culture goes beyond simple monetary transactions and can be said to be a custom showing the mutual aid tradition of Korean society.
B2:예전에는 겨울이 되면 온 가족과 이웃이 모여 함께 김치를 담그는 김: In the past, when winter came, Gimjang, where the whole family and neighbors gathered to make kimchi together, was a big event. Nowadays, instead of spending time and effort making it themselves, households purchasing commercial kimchi or packaged kimchi are increasing. Even so, Gimjang holds meaning not only as a task of preparing side dishes but also as a community event where family and neighbors share affection together. Instead of making it in large quantities, households that changed to making just as much as needed in small quantities have also increased. Local governments hold Gimjang sharing events, and activities delivering kimchi to vulnerable groups continue steadily. Ultimately, although the form of Gimjang culture has changed little by little, its original value of sharing and community spirit can still be said to continue.
B2:1인 가구가 늘어날수록 간편하게 한 끼를 해결할 수 있는 편의점 도: As single-person households increase, demand for convenience store lunchboxes that can conveniently solve a meal also grows together. As products collaborated with famous chefs are released, consumer perception of convenience store lunchboxes is also gradually changing positively. In that you can choose various menus at a low price, it is a practical choice for busy modern people. As competition becomes fierce, convenience stores are trying to use fresher and healthier ingredients. As various new products pour out, consumers' range of choices also widens together. Ultimately, the growth of the convenience store lunchbox market can be said to be a phenomenon showing changing dietary life and family types.
B2:가을이 되면 대학마다 며칠에 걸쳐 축제가 열리는데 이 시기에는 캠퍼: When autumn comes, festivals are held at universities over several days, and during this period, the whole campus is filled with vitality. Each department operates characteristic pubs or booths while preparing for the festival, creating opportunities to interact with students. Since stages inviting famous singers are bound to be held, many students eagerly wait for this period. While enjoying the festival with friends, there are many cases of meeting club seniors and juniors again after a long time. Since academic schedules naturally loosen somewhat during the festival period, it also becomes a time for recharging for students. Ultimately, university festivals can be said to be precious events where you can briefly put down academic stress and feel a sense of community.
B2:몇십 년 전만 해도 카페는 몇몇 큰 도시에만 있는 특별한 공간이었지: A few decades ago, cafes were special spaces existing only in a few big cities, but now franchise cafes can easily be found in every alley. Cafes are now spaces utilized for various purposes such as studying, working, and meetings, going beyond simply drinking coffee. Stores equipped with wide seats and power outlets have established themselves not only as popular workspaces for students and office workers but also as new meeting places. There are evaluations that the increase in franchise cafes did not just stop at commercial growth but changed the neighborhood scenery itself. Coffee culture not only reflects consumption trends but also changed people's lifestyles together. Ultimately, cafes can be said to have established themselves as central spaces of daily life all over the city.
B2:배달 애플리케이션에서는 음식을 주문한 소비자가 별점과 후기를 남기는: On delivery applications, a review system is operated where consumers who order food leave star ratings and reviews. If food arrives late or the condition is not good, consumers are bound to write complaints with low star ratings. If negative reviews accumulate, it can directly hit the store's sales, so bosses have no choice but to be sensitive to reviews. This structure helps raise service quality, but if malicious reviews are posted, small business owners are prone to suffer unfair damage. If stores inducing good evaluations with review events increase, the reliability of reviews itself is prone to shaking. Ultimately, the review system can be said to be a system that gives useful information to consumers while simultaneously holding various side effects.
B2:젊은 인구가 계속 도시로 빠져나가는 탓에 여러 지방 소도시는 인구: Because the young population continues to flow out to cities, many regional small cities are facing the crisis of extinction beyond population decrease. Due to the decreasing number of school students, elementary schools closing down are increasing every year. As the population decreases, commercial districts contract together, repeating a vicious cycle where the local economy loses vitality. Because infrastructure such as hospitals and public transportation is lacking, the younger generation tries to leave for cities even more. As the proportion of the elderly population increases, the region's self-sustainability inevitably weakens. Ultimately, unless the government and local governments improve jobs and residential conditions together, this extinction phenomenon is expected to continue.
B2:졸업 후 각자 흩어져 지내던 동창들이 온라인 채팅방을 통해 다시 연: Classmates who had scattered and lived separately after graduation have become frequently reconnected through online chat rooms. At first, it was about sharing regards, but as we frequently exchanged news, it developed into regular meetings. As people with similar hobbies gather in online communities, it naturally leads to offline gatherings. These online-based gatherings allow relationships to be maintained beyond physical distance. Since people with clear interests gather, they often form deep bonds even in a short time. Ultimately, online platforms act as a new connecting link reconnecting scattered ties.
B2:유연 근무제는 정해진 총 근무 시간을 채우는 한 출퇴근 시간을 직원: The flexible work system is a system allowing employees to adjust their commuting hours themselves as long as they fulfill the set total working hours. Companies often designate core working hours and require employees to work during those times. As long as work performance is maintained, managers tend not to interfere much in work methods. The intent of this system is to allow employees with personal circumstances such as childcare or commuting to adjust their times. Rules requiring meetings that need collaboration to share schedules in advance are prepared together. Ultimately, the flexible work system can be said to be an attempt to guarantee personal autonomy as much as possible as long as it does not harm organizational performance.
B2:기업들은 제품을 홍보하기 위해 팔로워가 많은 인플루언서에게 협찬을: To promote products, companies are actively utilizing marketing methods that provide sponsorships to influencers with many followers. Influencers not only introduce products naturally in daily life but also induce purchases based on trust relationships with followers. The more followers there are, the higher the advertising unit price naturally becomes. Since content that looks like honest reviews is often actually advertisements, consumers are bound to feel confused. Because of this problem, regulations clearly indicating that it is an advertisement have been prepared, and sanctions upon violation are also being strengthened. Ultimately, influencer marketing can be said to be an effective promotion means while simultaneously holding the task of transparency.
B2:최근 여러 동네 도서관에서는 사서를 거치지 않고 스스로 책을 빌리고: Recently, various neighborhood libraries introduced an unmanned checkout system allowing books to be borrowed and returned by oneself without going through a librarian. While tagging their membership cards, users can also immediately check their checkout history on the screen. In the past, checkout procedures were limited to taking place at the counter, but now reservations and extensions are also possible with smartphone applications. While putting books in the return box, many users also search for and reserve books to read next in advance. The system introduction did not just stop at reducing manpower but led to the effect of increasing operating hours. Ultimately, the unmanned checkout system can be said to be a change that simultaneously enhanced user convenience and library operational efficiency.
B2:채식 인구가 늘어나면서 도심 곳곳에 채식 전문 식당이 생겨나는 반면: While vegetarian specialty restaurants are appearing all over the city as the vegetarian population increases, there are still many areas where it is difficult to find vegetarian menus. Compared to large cities, the number of vegetarian restaurants is noticeably smaller in local areas. Products with vegan certification marks can be trusted for raw materials, whereas products without certification have the hassle of consumers having to check ingredients one by one. Compared to general restaurants, vegetarian specialty restaurants are often somewhat expensive, drawing criticism that accessibility drops. While vegetarianism is establishing itself as a lifestyle, prejudiced gazes still exist together. Ultimately, for vegetarian culture to spread more widely, accessibility and awareness improvement must be achieved together.
B2:공유 오피스는 여러 회사나 개인이 하나의 공간을 함께 사용하며 필요: Shared offices are operated in a way where multiple companies or individuals share a single space and pay costs only as much as needed. Users not only use desks and conference rooms but can also use auxiliary facilities like printers or coffee together. For startups in the early stages of founding, it is much less burdensome compared to renting a large office. Since people from various industries gather in one space, collaboration opportunities naturally arise and it also becomes a place for networking. The point that you can use spaces only for the period needed without a set contract period is also a flexible choice. Ultimately, shared offices can be said to have established themselves as practical alternatives tailored to changing working environments.
B2:전기차 보급이 계속 늘어나는 이상 이를 뒷받침할 충전소도 함께 확충: As the supply of electric vehicles continues to increase, voices are growing that charging stations supporting them must also be expanded. The more charging stations increase, the more the inconveniences of electric vehicle users will decrease accordingly. As the government and local governments install chargers in apartment complexes and public parking lots, accessibility is expected to improve gradually. The more fast chargers there are, the more consumers' anxiety about long-distance driving decreases. The hassle of having to plan charging in advance remains as long as you drive an electric vehicle in areas with insufficient infrastructure. Ultimately, expanding charging infrastructure can be said to be one of the most important tasks accelerating the popularization of electric vehicles.
B2:신입사원 연수는 보통 회사의 조직 문화를 익히는 데다가 실무 기초를: New employee training usually consists of learning the company's organizational culture and learning the basics of actual work. Companies often conduct teamwork activities together so that new employees can get close to each other. Because it proceeds with an intense schedule and has to run presentations or tasks in parallel, it is also a physically difficult period. A system where senior employees are assigned as mentors to help new employees adapt quickly is also operated together. Programs experiencing various departments and also executing projects close to actual work are increasing. Ultimately, the training process can be said to be an important first step allowing new employees to naturally melt into the organization.
B2:아파트에서 층간소음 문제가 발생할 경우 주민들은 먼저 관리사무소를: When floor-noise problems occur in apartments, residents often first deliver the situation through the management office. Since emotions are bound to become intense if neighbors talk directly, using mediation institutions is also increasing. If the problem is not resolved, applications for mediation can be filed with official institutions like the Environmental Dispute Adjustment Commission. If noise measurement results exceed standard levels, compensation orders are sometimes issued. Since older conflicts tend to deepen emotional rifts, trying dialogue early is important. Ultimately, floor-noise problems can be said to be fundamentally resolvable only when institutional procedures are accompanied by consideration between neighbors.
B2:한국의 웹툰은 스마트폰으로 세로로 스크롤하며 볼 수 있는 형식으로: Korean webtoons started in a format that could be viewed by scrolling vertically on smartphones and have now become content loved worldwide. Webtoon platforms not only provide serialization opportunities to rookie authors but also act as communication channels with readers. In the early days, it stopped at gathering readers with free content, but now it has grown into an industry encompassing paid payments and advertising revenue. Popular webtoons are produced into dramas or movies and are also translated and exported to various countries overseas. The growth of the industry does not stop at simple content consumption but leads to derivative businesses like related goods and pop-up stores. Ultimately, webtoons can be said to have established themselves as Korea's representative cultural content industry.
B2:지역 축제는 짧은 기간 동안 많은 방문객을 끌어모으는 만큼 지역 상: As regional festivals attract many visitors for a short period, they bring immediate economic effects to local commercial districts. Accommodation establishments and restaurants must prepare in advance to accommodate visitors even if they flock during the festival period. As booths selling regional specialties increase, new sales channels are also opened for small business owners. Even if the weather is bad, if interesting programs are prepared, the number of visitors tends not to decrease significantly. As the scale of festivals grows, the local government's budget burden also grows together in reality. Ultimately, regional festivals can be said to contribute not only to short-term economic effects but also to enhancing regional brand value.
B2:육아휴직은 만 여덟 살 이하의 자녀를 둔 근로자가 일정 기간 회사를: Parental leave is a system allowing workers with children aged eight or younger to rest from the company for a certain period and take care of children. Workers are required to submit application forms in writing at least thirty days in advance. If the company rejects applications without justifiable reasons, it may receive legal sanctions. The government operates policies supporting a portion of wages so that there are no livelihood difficulties during the leave period. If spouses share and use the period, each can also receive parental leave benefits separately. Ultimately, this system can be said to act as a social safety net allowing parents to balance work and childcare.
B2:명절이 다가오면 고향으로 향하는 사람들로 기차역과 버스터미널이 붐비: When holidays approach, train stations and bus terminals are bound to be crowded with people heading to their hometowns. Because of the excitement of meeting family after a long time, you can see people whose steps are light despite carrying heavy luggage. Train tickets are bound to sell out simultaneously with the start of booking, so people flocking in front of booking counters from days before is common. Homecoming roads not only take several hours, but the scenery of long lines stretching at each rest area in the middle is also common. As people preparing gift sets before holidays increase, marts and markets are bound to be crowded together. Ultimately, despite being a difficult and cumbersome journey, you can see many people willingly taking this road every year because of the joy of meeting family.
A1:네, 좋아요! 몇 시에 만날까요?: Yes, sounds good! What time shall we meet?
I am reading a book right now.

Thank you! I am going to have dinner with my family today.

B2:저는 주 4일 근무제 도입에 찬성하는 편이다. 근무 일수를 하루 줄: I am generally in favor of introducing a 4-day workweek. If we reduce the number of workdays by one, it is like securing time for employees to recharge, so concentration can actually increase during the remaining four days. Looking at various experimental introduction cases, it is said that not only does productivity not drop, but in many cases it actually improves. Of course, there are concerns that reducing a day could cause labor shortage problems depending on the industry, but I think it is a problem that can be sufficiently overcome if work methods are streamlined. In particular, for employees balancing childcare or nursing, having an extra day of leisure is like greatly improving their quality of life. If a full introduction is difficult right now, there might also be a way to expand it step by step through pilot operations. In the end, I think a 4-day workweek is the direction that benefits both workers and companies.
B2:나는 완전 원격근무보다 하이브리드 근무가 더 낫다고 생각한다. 완전: I think hybrid work is better than completely remote work. While completely remote work saves commuting time, the opportunities for impromptu communication with colleagues are greatly reduced. Compared to going to the office every day, if you only go to the office two or three days a week, you can handle tasks that require concentration at home and tasks that require collaboration in the office. Of course, completely remote work has the advantage of maximizing personal autonomy, but for new employees, it becomes much harder to adapt to the organizational culture. On the other hand, I think the hybrid approach is a balancing point where you can secure both autonomy and a sense of belonging at the same time. From a manager's perspective as well, hybrid work is a bit easier to manage teamwork than completely remote work. Therefore, I think many companies will continue to adopt the hybrid approach as a standard in the future.
B2:나는 한국 식당에 팁 문화를 새롭게 도입하는 것에는 반대하는 입장이: I am against newly introducing a tipping culture in Korean restaurants. If tips become established like an obligation, customers are bound to worry about how much they should give every time they calculate the bill. Also, if employee income depends on tips, the quality of service is bound to vary depending on the customer's mood or personal connections. Of course, there are countries like America where tips support the livelihood of servers, but this is merely the result of a structure where base pay was designed low from the beginning. In Korea, service charges are already included in the price in many cases, so adding tips is bound to be like imposing a double burden. I think the direction of rather improving employees' base pay and treatment is bound to be fairer for both customers and employees. Therefore, I think settling a fair wage system is a priority over a tipping culture.
B2:나는 AI가 채용 과정 전체를 좌우하는 것에는 신중해야 한다고 본다: I think we need to be cautious about AI dominating the entire hiring process. While AI can process thousands of applications in a short time, it often fails to properly read the individual context or special career history of each applicant. In particular, applicants with career gaps can be filtered out disadvantageously in the AI system. Of course, we cannot deny that AI greatly increases efficiency in repetitive stages like initial document screening, but I think leaving even the final judgment up to AI is dangerous. While in-person interviews conducted by humans take a long time, they have the advantage of being able to examine subtle parts such as the applicant's attitude and potential. Ultimately, I think AI should be used as a tool to assist the hiring process and should not become the final decision-maker. Therefore, I think a cooperative method where humans and AI divide roles is the most desirable.
B2:나는 인기 관광지의 방문객 수를 제한하는 정책에 찬성한다. 과도한: I am in favor of policies that limit the number of visitors to popular tourist destinations. Excessive tourists not only make the daily lives of local residents inconvenient, but also rapidly damage historical sites and the natural environment. If the daily admission cap is limited, it is like each visitor can enjoy the tourist spot more leisurely, so satisfaction can actually increase. Of course, there are counterarguments that reducing the number of tourists could reduce the short-term income of local commercial districts, but I think preserving the value of the tourist destination in the long run leads to sustainable profit. Introducing a reservation system or differential admission fees is also like gaining the effect of dispersing the visiting period. It is also worth considering that several countries are already implementing such systems and obtaining successful results. Therefore, I think tourist limits are not a simple regulation, but an essential measure to protect tourist spots.
B2:나는 외국인의 국내 부동산 투자를 어느 정도 제한할 필요가 있다고: I think there is a need to limit real estate investment by foreigners in Korea to some extent. Because speculative funds flock in, domestic buyers who are actual end-users have no choice but to bear the rise in house prices as it is. In particular, apartments in popular areas often see abnormally rising prices because foreign capital even jumps into the competition. Of course, foreign investment has positive aspects of supplying liquidity to the real estate market and vitalizing some local economies, but if those profits do not return to local residents, the meaning is bound to fade. Therefore, I think a method of heavily taxing speculative purchases that are not for actual residence purposes is necessary. This way, without completely blocking the market, it will have no choice but to calm down the overheating to some extent. In the end, I think we must not forget that real estate is a living space where people must live before it is an investment product.
B2:나는 소셜미디어에 최소 연령 제한을 두는 정책에 찬성한다. 나이가: I am in favor of a policy that sets a minimum age limit on social media. The younger they are, the more they are swayed by online comparisons and malicious comments, making them emotionally vulnerable and easily hurt. If we stop at relying only on autonomous age verification as we do now, children and teenagers can still easily create accounts and use them. Of course, there are counterarguments that age limits restrict freedom of expression, but I think protecting mental health during the growing years is more important. Research results showing that side effects like sleep deprivation and lowered concentration increase together as usage time gets longer also support this argument. I think the key is to not just stop at checking age, but to prepare an authentication system that can actually verify it. In the end, I think an age limit, even if not a perfect solution, is a definitely necessary minimum safety device.
B2:나는 일회용 플라스틱을 전면적으로 금지하는 정책에 원칙적으로 찬성한: I am in principle in favor of a policy that completely bans disposable plastics. Plastics take hundreds of years to decompose and furthermore flow into the ocean to threaten marine ecosystems. With autonomous regulation alone, even if usage decreases little by little, it is bound to eventually stagnate at a certain level. Of course, there are concerns that a sudden total ban could put a burden on small business owners or consumers who find it hard to get substitutes, but giving a sufficient grace period can reduce that shock. While there are also criticisms that the initial cost of converting to paper or biodegradable materials is burdensome and quality is not yet fully satisfactory, technology is bound to develop together as the market grows. Ultimately, I think companies are bound to invest seriously in developing substitutes only when there is strong regulation. Therefore, I think a step-by-step but clear roadmap for a total ban is necessary.
B2:나는 대중교통 요금을 한꺼번에 큰 폭으로 인상하는 것에는 신중해야: I think we should be cautious about raising public transportation fares by a large margin all at once. As long as operating deficits continue to pile up, a certain level of fare increase may be inevitable. However, if fares rise too much at once, the burden on low-income groups and workers who commute frequently increases rapidly. Of course, I acknowledge that keeping fares continuously low is bound to lead to facility aging and lowered service quality. Nevertheless, as long as finances are really difficult, I think we should consider other methods together, such as expanding government subsidies as well as raising fares. If fares are raised little by little over multiple times, the shock received by citizens will also be much smaller. Therefore, I think a gradual and predictable adjustment is desirable rather than a sudden increase.
B2:나는 기본소득 제도의 도입에 조심스럽게 찬성하는 입장이다. 모든 국: I am cautiously in favor of introducing a basic income system. Providing a minimum living expense to all citizens is like preventing extreme poverty, so it can greatly reduce the blind spots of the social safety net. This not only stops at helping low-income groups, but also serves as a minimum buffer for people losing jobs to automation. Of course, I can fully understand concerns about how to secure massive financial resources and whether it will lower the willingness to work. However, looking at various experiment results, it is also worth noting that people who received basic income often tried new challenges instead. If we reorganize the tax system together, securing resources is not only an impossible task, but it is also like becoming an opportunity to sort out the inefficiencies of existing welfare systems. Therefore, I think starting from small-scale pilot projects and expanding gradually is realistic.
B2:나는 자율주행차의 확산이 필요하다고 보지만 완전한 대체는 신중하게: I think the spread of self-driving cars is necessary, but approaching complete replacement should be done with caution. While autonomous driving technology reduces accidents caused by human error, it is prone to lacking judgment in unpredictable unexpected situations. In particular, cases are still being reported where the system is prone to malfunctioning in sudden pedestrian appearances or bad weather situations. Of course, the outlook that technology will develop in the long run and safety will become much higher than humans is also valid. However, while the jobs of numerous people making a living as drivers suddenly disappear, transition to new jobs is prone to happening slowly. Therefore, I think the transition to fully autonomous driving must be accompanied by job transition support along with safety verification. Ultimately, I think it is desirable to introduce it step by step over time so that society can keep up with the speed of technological development.
B2:나는 원자력 발전을 제한적으로나마 친환경 에너지원으로 인정할 필요가: I think there is a need to recognize nuclear power as an eco-friendly energy source, even if limitedly. Compared to thermal power generation, nuclear power not only has significantly lower greenhouse gas emissions, but also has much higher power generation efficiency. The fact that it can supply power stably regardless of weather or seasons compared to solar or wind power is also a big advantage. Of course, the problem of radioactive waste disposal and the risk in case of an accident are serious disadvantages that can never be taken lightly. Nevertheless, we need to consider that it is realistically difficult to cover all immediate power demand with renewable energy alone, and its role as a transitional energy source cannot be ignored. If safety standards are strengthened much more strictly than now, I think accident risks are at a relatively manageable level compared to fossil fuels. Therefore, I think utilizing nuclear power under the condition of running parallel with the expansion of renewable energy is a realistic choice.
B2:나는 채용 공고에 급여 범위를 반드시 공개하도록 하는 제도에 찬성한: I am in favor of a system that makes it mandatory to disclose the salary range in job postings. Right now, applicants only find out the salary after finishing interviews, whereas disclosing the salary in advance can save time and effort. In particular, while disadvantageous conditions are presented to applicants with relatively weak bargaining power like women or career-interrupted persons, if salaries are transparently disclosed, such inequality can be reduced. Making companies specify salaries makes the hiring process much more efficient. Of course, I can understand the company's perspective that they might be reluctant to have information exposed to competitors. However, many countries already make salary disclosure mandatory by law, and it is evaluated that positive functions are greater than side effects. Therefore, I think Korea should also move in the direction of making salary disclosure mandatory step by step.
B2:나는 현금을 완전히 없애는 것에는 반대하는 입장이다. 디지털 결제가: I am against completely getting rid of cash. As much as digital payments are convenient, if a blackout or system error occurs, the risk of the entire society becoming paralyzed also increases together. No matter how stable technology is, the elderly or people unfamiliar with digital devices are bound to remain alienated. Of course, as cash usage decreases, tracking tax evasion and crime funds becomes easier, so there is a clear advantage, and the direction itself cannot be denied. However, concerns about privacy infringement are also quite large in terms of personal information and consumption history all remaining on record. No matter how popular card or mobile payments become, I think a minimum cash payment method must be left. Therefore, I think the direction where cash and digital payments coexist is safer than a completely cashless society.
B2:나는 AI가 만든 창작물에 저작권을 인정하는 것에는 제한적으로 접근: I think we should approach recognizing copyright for creations made by AI with limitations. AI learns works of existing creators to make new results, and in this process, the rights of original creators are not being sufficiently protected, I believe. Granting copyright wholly to AI itself not only blurs the essence of creative acts, but can also threaten the market for human creators. Of course, if a person utilizes AI as a tool to delicately design prompts and edit the results, I think there is a need to recognize that person's creative contribution. In such cases, copyright cannot be completely denied, and I think the creator's effort must also be respected. Ultimately, I think copyright should be judged according to the degree of creative intervention by the person who utilized it, not AI itself. Therefore, I think it is necessary to prepare specific criteria rather than uniform regulations for this issue.
B2:나는 정년퇴직 제도를 완전히 없애는 것에는 신중해야 한다고 생각한다: I think we should be cautious about completely abolishing the retirement age system. If the retirement age is abolished, it is like capable older workforce gets the advantage of having the opportunity to keep working. But at the same time, if the retirement age disappears, the risk of hiring opportunities for new recruits and the younger generation decreasing also grows together. Of course, I also agree with the principle that evaluation should be based solely on ability, but in reality, implicit discrimination based on age still exists. Rather than completely abolishing the retirement age, I think a method of letting them continue to work through re-employment or contract work even after a certain age is more realistic. By doing this, it can be like maintaining the metabolism of the organization while also utilizing experienced personnel. Therefore, I think expanding a flexible re-employment system is a more desirable direction than abolishing the retirement age.
B2:나는 자동차나 가전제품을 구독하는 방식이 앞으로 더 확산될 것이라고: I view positively that the method of subscribing to cars or home appliances will spread more in the future. Instead of spending a large sum to purchase them, paying a certain amount every month frees you from the burden of breakdowns or maintenance, making it convenient. In particular, in the case of home appliances where new products are released quickly, purchasing them quickly makes them old models, so subscription can be more rational. Of course, calculated in the long run, there is also the clear disadvantage that subscription fees can become more expensive than purchase costs. Beyond just saving costs, I think the flexibility of easily changing products according to need is also a big charm of subscription. Especially for people who move often or whose lifestyles change frequently, a subscription method that goes beyond just owning and lets you choose according to the situation is bound to be much more practical. Therefore, I think the concept of ownership gradually changing to the concept of usage is a natural flow.
B2:나는 긱 이코노미 노동자에게도 최소한의 사회적 보호 장치가 필요하다: I think gig economy workers also need a minimum social protection device. They not only work every day taking accident risks, but their income also fluctuates greatly depending on the weather or order volume. Without a minimum safety net like industrial accident compensation insurance or employment insurance, individuals have no choice but to shoulder all costs when an accident happens. Of course, the flexibility that they can work freely at times they want is a big advantage of the gig economy, and I can also understand the opinion that this should not be damaged. However, flexibility and a minimum safety net are not things that cannot coexist, and several countries have already prepared and implemented compromise solutions. If platform companies do not share social insurance premiums to a certain extent, that burden is bound to return to individual workers in the end. Therefore, I think an institutional compromise that guarantees minimum rights while maintaining flexibility is necessary.
B2:나는 온실가스를 많이 배출하는 기업에 탄소세를 부과하는 정책에 찬성: I am in favor of policies imposing a carbon tax on companies that emit a lot of greenhouse gases. I think that because companies have not properly borne the cost of emissions up until now, the entire society has shouldered the price of environmental pollution. The higher the carbon tax is set, the stronger the motivation companies are bound to have to reduce emissions. Of course, the concern that product prices will rise if the tax burden increases and that burden can be passed on to consumers is also valid. However, the reality that investment in eco-friendly technology continues to be delayed due to loose regulations is also a reality that cannot be ignored. If funds raised through the carbon tax are used to develop renewable energy or support vulnerable classes, the justification of the policy will grow stronger as side effects are reduced and effects are maximized. Therefore, I think a carbon tax is a policy that is definitely necessary in the long run despite short-term burdens.
B2:나는 공공장소의 CCTV 확대 설치에 조건부로 찬성한다. 범죄 예방: I am conditionally in favor of expanding the installation of CCTVs in public places. As long as the purpose of crime prevention is clear, expanding CCTV practically helps citizen safety. As long as the government clearly regulates the filming purpose and retention period, concerns about privacy infringement can also be controlled to some extent. Of course, criticism that excessive surveillance can shrink individual freedom is also quite valid. However, as long as access rights are strictly limited and out-of-purpose use is prohibited by law, side effects can be minimized. In fact, cases where the crime rate is lower in areas where many CCTVs are installed have been reported multiple times. Therefore, as long as transparent operating principles are kept, I think expanding CCTV can be a reasonable safety and freedom balancing point.
B2:나는 온라인 리뷰가 소상공인의 생계를 좌우할 정도로 큰 영향력을 갖: I think there is a problem with the current structure where online reviews have enough influence to determine the livelihood of small business owners. Seeing sales shake over a single review, owners often end up overly hanging on to review management. Just one malicious review left by an emotional customer is prone to instantly destroying a reputation built over a long time. Of course, I also acknowledge that the review system has the positive function of providing useful information to consumers and raising service quality. However, leaving unverified reviews alone makes them prone to being helplessly hit by false reviews or malicious attacks from competitors. If platforms do not strengthen procedures to verify the truth of reviews, I think such damages are bound to keep repeating. Therefore, I think a system is needed where consumers' right to know and the protection of small business owners can be achieved together.
B2:나는 도심 진입 차량에 혼잡통행료를 부과하는 정책에 찬성한다. 통행: I am in favor of a policy that imposes a congestion toll on vehicles entering downtown. When tolls are imposed, traffic volume in the city center decreases, so we can expect the effect of air pollution and noise decreasing together. This system not only eases traffic congestion, but also naturally increases the use of public transportation. Of course, it is true that it becomes an additional economic burden for people who have to commute by car. However, considering that the costs borne by the entire society also increase as congestion gets worse, imposing tolls is a reasonable choice. If collected tolls are reinvested into expanding public transportation, it will not only ease fairness issues but also raise citizens' support for the policy. Therefore, I think this policy should be expanded on the premise of transparent use of toll revenues.
B2:나는 AI 챗봇이 고객센터 상담원을 전면적으로 대체하는 것에는 반대: I am against AI chatbots completely replacing customer center agents. While chatbots respond quickly to simple and repetitive questions, they are bound to reveal limits in front of complex and emotional problems. For example, in situations tangled with emotions like refunds or disputes, human agent empathy is necessary, but it is hard for chatbots to replace this part. Of course, consumer convenience certainly increases in that utilizing chatbots greatly reduces waiting times and enables 24-hour response, but agent jobs are bound to decrease correspondingly. If it is a dualized structure where simple inquiries are handled by chatbots and complex issues are passed to humans, I think we can bring out the advantages of both methods. When companies introduce chatbots aiming solely at cost reduction, customer satisfaction is bound to drop instead. Therefore, I think chatbots should be used as an auxiliary means, and the role of human agents should not be completely eliminated.
B2:나는 직원들이 연차를 반드시 소진하도록 하는 제도에 찬성한다. 연차: I am in favor of a system that makes employees thoroughly use their annual leave. If annual leave is left to autonomy, people often end up not using it and letting it expire because they mind others' opinions. If companies have employees submit annual leave usage plans in advance, it is like making employees manage their rest time methodically on their own. Of course, there are counterarguments that being forced to rest during busy work periods can feel burdensome instead. But in the long run, sufficient rest eventually leads to higher productivity, so it is beneficial to the company as well. If managers are made to regularly check the annual leave usage rate by department, the culture of minding others' opinions will also naturally decrease. Therefore, I think the mandatory annual leave usage system is a method that protects individual quality of life and organizational sustainability together.
B2:나는 임대료 상한제 도입에 조심스럽게 찬성하는 입장이다. 임대료가: I am cautiously in favor of introducing a rent cap system. If rents rise significantly every year, tenants are forced to repeat moving every few years, making life unstable. Introducing a cap will be able to prevent such sudden increases to some extent, helping tenants' housing stability. Of course, there are also valid concerns that if the cap is applied too strictly, landlords might not put properties on the market at all, reducing supply instead. In fact, some cities had no choice but to experience side effects where new rental supplies decreased after the rent cap. Therefore, I think meticulous design is necessary, such as introducing the cap while exempting new construction or housing under specific conditions. Ultimately, the rent cap alone cannot solve all problems, but I think it can produce sufficient effect if implemented together with supply expansion policies.
B2:나는 청년층에게 코리빙 하우스가 전통적인 자취 생활보다 여러 면에서: I think co-living houses are a more realistic alternative than traditional living alone for the younger generation in many aspects. Compared to finding a one-room studio alone, the burden of deposit and monthly rent in co-living houses is much smaller. While personal space is narrow, living costs can be greatly reduced by sharing common spaces like kitchens or lounges. Of course, there will definitely be people who feel uncomfortable sharing space with strangers or feel their privacy is infringed. However, compared to living completely alone, the fact that opportunities to naturally interact with people arise can be a big advantage, especially for young people who came from other regions. While freedom in personal space decreases somewhat, the emotional benefit of feeling less lonely and being able to share information cannot be ignored. Therefore, I think co-living houses need to spread more widely as an alternative to youth housing problems.
I think regulations on electric kickboards should be strengthened more than now. Because helmet wearing or license verification is not properly done, when accidents happen, the degree of injury is bound to become serious. Because of kickboards left abandoned anywhere on sidewalks, accidents where pedestrians, especially the visually impaired or elderly, trip over them happen frequently, and safety issues continue to be raised. Of course, we cannot deny that kickboards are a very convenient transportation means when moving short distances. However, because regulations are loose, minors utilizing them without a license also happens commonly. If parking zones are clearly designated and fines are strengthened upon violation, these problems are bound to decrease to some extent. Therefore, I think minimum regulations for safety are definitely necessary while maintaining the convenience of kickboards.
B2:나는 실질적인 변화 없이 이미지만 친환경적으로 포장하는 그린워싱에: I am strongly critical of greenwashing, which packages an image as eco-friendly without substantial changes. Many companies often end up just putting up eco-friendly fronts on the outside while not changing actual production methods or raw materials at all. Such marketing not only deceives consumers, but also drags down the credibility of eco-friendly companies that are genuinely trying. Of course, I can understand that it is hard for all companies to practice eco-friendly management perfectly from the start and that they are in a process of gradual change. But if they just stop at dazzling consumers with exaggerated expressions in advertisements, I consider this clear consumer deception. I think the government should strictly prepare eco-friendly labeling criteria, penalize violations, and demand transparent disclosure of labeling grounds. Therefore, I think legal and institutional devices to prevent greenwashing must be urgently prepared.
B2:나는 재택근무를 완전히 폐지하고 전면 출근을 강제하는 방침에는 동의: It is hard for me to agree with policies that completely abolish work-from-home and force full-time office attendance. I think several companies have already proven since the pandemic that sufficient performance can be achieved even with remote work. If returning to the office is suddenly forced, employees who have coordinated for a long time due to childcare or commuting issues are bound to experience big confusion. Of course, I think tasks requiring new employee training or creative collaboration are more effective when conducted in-person. However, forcing all tasks to be handled uniformly only in the office is an excessive measure. As superior talent values flexibility more, forced office attendance policies are bound to lead to brain drain in the end. Therefore, I think it is more reasonable to let work methods be chosen flexibly according to work characteristics.
I think subscription to industrial accident compensation insurance should be made mandatory for delivery workers. They work every day on roads chasing time, and even if an accident happens, without insurance, it is like bearing all treatment costs themselves. If a major accident occurs while not enrolled in industrial accident compensation insurance, even the livelihood of the worker and their family can be shaken. Of course, due to the characteristic of delivery workers utilizing multiple platforms simultaneously, there are practical difficulties that insurance premium calculation and enrollment procedures are complex. Postponing this problem continuously even so is, in the end, passing the risk onto the most vulnerable workers. If a system where platform companies share insurance premiums in proportion to the number of deliveries is introduced, these difficulties can also be solved to a large extent. Therefore, I think making industrial accident compensation insurance mandatory is a task that can no longer be delayed.
B2:나는 업무용 이메일이나 보고서 작성에 AI 도구를 활용하는 것에 대: I am generally positive about utilizing AI tools for writing work emails or reports. Utilizing AI not only greatly reduces time spent on repetitive document tasks, but can also refine sentences more clearly and concisely. Writing done in a hurry while chased by time is bound to mix typos or awkward expressions, but going through AI tools can reduce these mistakes to a large extent. Of course, the concern that if you just keep copy-pasting sentences written by AI, your own writing style or judgment can gradually dull is also valid. In particular, leaving documents containing sensitive content or important decision-making entirely to AI is bound to lead to misunderstandings or information leaks. Therefore, I think AI should be utilized as an auxiliary tool to draft or refine expressions, and final review must definitely be done by humans directly. Ultimately, I think AI tools are useful means to raise work efficiency, but their use requires a clear line.
B2:나는 디지털 노마드 비자 제도의 확대에 긍정적인 입장이다. 이 제도: I am in favor of expanding the digital nomad visa system. This system gives remote workers the opportunity to stay legally in a new country, and furthermore breathes life into the local economy of that country. As the countries introducing nomad visas increase, talented individuals can move freely and build diverse experiences. Of course, tax issues or fairness issues with the local labor market are not completely resolved, and regulations differ by country, making it confusing in parts. However, as such systems become active, life options become much wider for people in job groups capable of remote work. From the local perspective as well, people who came through nomad visas increase consumption and can even gain the effect of naturally promoting local culture abroad. Therefore, I think each country should continue to expand this system while organizing clear tax and labor regulations.
B2:나는 국민연금 수급 연령을 점진적으로 상향 조정하는 것에 어느 정도: I somewhat agree with raising the national pension receipt age gradually. As average life expectancy continues to increase, if the current receipt age is maintained as is, pension finances are bound to be depleted someday. As long as the population structure ages, the share that the younger generation must bear is a reality that is bound to keep growing. Of course, as the period without income after retirement gets longer, I can also fully understand the counterargument that delaying the receipt age makes immediate livelihood harder. Therefore, as much as adjusting the receipt age, I think extending the retirement age or re-employment systems should also be discussed together. Unless these two are promoted together, the post-retirement income gap is bound to lead to more serious problems. Therefore, I think how to fill the gap between retirement and pension receipt is a more important discussion than the age adjustment itself.
B2:나는 카페나 식당의 야외 좌석을 포함해 실외 흡연을 전면 금지하는: I am generally in favor of policies completely banning outdoor smoking, including outdoor seating at cafes or restaurants. Cigarette smoke not only harms the health of the smoker, but also gives secondhand smoke damage to non-smokers nearby. Even outdoors, smoke easily spreads in seats where people are crowded, so it is hard to block damage without a complete cutoff. Of course, opinions that smokers' personal freedom and choice should be respected are also quite valid. However, at the point where individual freedom infringes on others' right to health, restrictions are inevitable, and social consensus has already leaned in that direction. If designated smoking areas are prepared sufficiently, smokers' inconvenience can also be reduced to some extent. Therefore, I think a total outdoor smoking ban is not ignoring smokers' rights, but a reasonable measure for coexistence.
B2:나는 법정 음주 가능 연령을 지금보다 높이는 방안에 신중하게 찬성하: I am cautiously in favor of raising the legal drinking age higher than now. While starting to drink at a young age doesn't seem to cause big physical problems, brain development has not completely ended at that age, so long-term effects can be much bigger. Compared to other adult activities, drinking should be approached more cautiously in that it has an immediate effect on judgment and physical control ability. Of course, I also understand the counterargument that suddenly raising the already established age could cause fairness controversies. But compared to cases in other countries, we also need to take to heart the point that Korea has a culture relatively lenient toward alcohol. While there is also a method of strengthening education and campaigns instead of raising the age, I think there are limits to improving awareness without institutional devices. Therefore, I think raising the age must be accompanied by social awareness improvement regarding the drinking reduction culture.
B2:나는 주말마다 도심 일부 구간을 차 없는 거리로 운영하는 정책에 찬: I am in favor of operating some sections of downtown as car-free streets every weekend. When vehicle entry is blocked, downtown turns into a human-centered space for that time, so it can breathe life into commercial districts as well. In fact, as multiple cities implemented such policies, there were many cases where floating populations of cafes and restaurants actually increased. Of course, we must also consider that inconvenience can occur for merchants or nearby residents who have to move by car. But if alternative parking spaces and shuttle buses are prepared together, that inconvenience is something that can be sufficiently reduced. As people walk around and enjoy the streets, consumption naturally increases, and there is an effect where local cultural events are revitalized together. Therefore, I think expanding pedestrian-only downtown streets will bring positive changes both commercially and environmentally.
I think we should be cautious about policies making public transportation completely free. Eliminating fares is attractive in that it can be expected to have the effect of not only increasing users in the short term, but also reducing private car use. Making it free not only guarantees the mobility rights of low-income groups, but can also widen social participation opportunities for the transportation vulnerable. Of course, practical problems like where to finance the resources still remain. In some cities that implemented free rides, the initial expected effects did not last long, and there were cases where congestion only increased instead. Therefore, rather than making it completely free, a method of exempting fares for specific classes like low-income groups or the elderly can reduce financial burden and also raise policy sustainability. Ultimately, I think staged and selective support is a more realistic alternative than total free rides.
I am against unconditionally increasing the notice period before resignation. If the notice period is too short, handovers are not properly done, so remaining team members suffer difficulties, which is true. However, if the notice period is excessively increased, employees whose hearts have already left are bound to guard their positions formally during the remaining period. Of course, I can also understand the company's perspective that sufficient time must be secured to hire a new person and smoothly continue work. Even so, forcibly increasing the notice period by several months at a time leads to results restricting individual job change decision rights themselves. Rather, if work manuals are organized well ordinarily and manpower is operated with leisure, we will be able to cope without big confusion even in a short notice period. Therefore, I think improving the organization's response system is a more fundamental solution than increasing the notice period.
B2:나는 도심 지역의 단기 임대 서비스를 지금보다 엄격하게 규제해야 한: I think short-term rental services in downtown areas should be regulated more strictly than now. Because short-term rentals targeting tourists are increasing, people who actually want to reside in that area are finding it increasingly difficult to find rental properties. This phenomenon not only threatens the housing stability of local residents, but also heightens noise and safety issues of the entire apartment complex as well. Of course, I can also understand the realistic reason from the landlord's perspective that short-term rentals are much more profitable than long-term rentals. However, because short-term rentals concentrate in specific areas, the side effect where the rental market for actual residence purposes shrinks cannot be ignored. If a registration system is introduced and the number of days operable per year is limited, tourism demand can be accommodated to some extent, and distortions in the housing market can also be reduced. Therefore, I think minimum regulations to prevent reckless expansion are definitely necessary.
B2:나는 플라스틱병 보증금 반환제를 전국적으로 확대 시행해야 한다고 생: I think the plastic bottle deposit return system should be expanded and implemented nationwide. When consumers return bottles and get their deposits back, it is practically like receiving a small reward for recycling. As more people participate, the recovery rate rises, and the amount of plastic that needs to be newly produced decreases correspondingly. Of course, there are also practical difficulties that installing and operating unmanned collection machines everywhere costs significant initial expenses. But looking at countries already implementing this system, recovery rates exceed 90 percent, so the effect has been clearly proven. As participants increase, social awareness of the deposit system will also naturally settle in. Therefore, considering long-term environmental effects even if we endure initial investment costs, I think it is well worth implementing nationwide.
C1:이사 온 지 벌써 일주일이 지났는데도 골목마다 여전히 낯설게 느껴진: A week has already passed since I moved, but every alley still feels unfamiliar. While I feel sad about leaving my dear old neighborhood, the excitement of starting over in a new place is slowly taking root. Today, I went into a nearby cafe and had a short chat with the owner, which made this place feel a little comfortable for the first time. Not a single road was familiar, so I couldn't even walk without a map for a few days. Still, the fun of discovering unfamiliar scenery in a new way every day feels like an unexpected gift. These small coincidences will pile up, and someday this neighborhood will surely feel like my own.
C1:오늘 우연히 옛날 사진을 정리하다가 예전에 정말 친했던 친구의 얼굴: Today, while randomly sorting through old pictures, I faced the face of a friend who was once really close to me after a long time. As we each lived busy lives, it has already been over three years since we lost touch. It wasn't anyone's fault, so the fact that we just naturally grew distant feels a bit sad, but on the other hand, it seems natural. In the past, I thought it would be a huge deal if we didn't contact each other every day, but thinking about it now, it seems like we were just a relationship fitting that time. Still, seeing how I suddenly miss those days, my friend must still remain in a corner of my heart. Tonight, I think I should send a short greeting message after a long time.
C1:드디어 오늘 새 회사에서 첫 출근을 했다. 낯선 얼굴들과 낯선 자리: Finally, I had my first day at my new company today. My body and mind are exhausted because I was nervous all day long with unfamiliar faces and an unfamiliar seating arrangement. Not only do I need to learn new tasks, but I also have to figure out people's names and personalities, so my head feels full of information. Fortunately, the colleague next to me kindly explained this and that, so I felt a bit relieved. Since today is like writing the first sentence of a new beginning, I don't think I need to rush too much. I hope I can smile a little more naturally tomorrow than today.
C1:오늘 본가에 다녀왔는데 아버지의 걸음이 예전보다 눈에 띄게 느려지신: I visited my parents' home today and noticed that my father's walk has noticeably slowed down compared to before. I always considered him a reliable and strong person, so I think I lived without even realizing that time passes like that. Seeing the white hair of my mother sitting at the dining table, I felt the weight of that time all over again. When I was young, I thought my parents would stay just like that forever, but now I know how naive that thought was. All the way back home, my heart was heavy, but at the same time, I also made up my mind to visit them more often. Next weekend, I must make time to spend a relaxing day with my parents.
C1:서랍을 정리하다가 오 년 전에 쓰던 일기장을 발견해서 무심코 펼쳐: While organizing my drawer, I found a diary I used five years ago and opened it absentmindedly. Unlike back then when I took things so seriously as if the world was ending, reading it again now, most of those worries were no big deal. By meeting myself from that time like this, I felt that my worries today will also someday become this light. Even in the clumsy sentences, I could feel the genuine feelings unique to that time, which made me chuckle. I could also confirm once again that I have become a little tougher than I was back then. I make up my mind to write in my diary consistently starting from today.
C1:오늘 드디어 사직서를 제출했다. 안정적인 급여와 익숙한 업무를 포기: Today, I finally submitted my resignation letter. It would be a lie to say I wasn't afraid of giving up a stable salary and familiar work. However, since this job doesn't just stop at making money but fills most of my day, I couldn't force myself to endure it anymore. For months, I worried every night and crunched the numbers, but in the end, I couldn't ignore the direction my heart was heading. People around me gave me a lot of worried words, but strangely, I feel at ease just for today. Things won't be smooth sailing ahead, but I believe this is a choice that will leave me with no regrets, at least.
C1:결혼식을 한 달 앞두고 요즘 매일 밤 마음이 복잡하다. 평생을 함께: A month before the wedding, my mind is complicated every night these days. While I am excited about the fact that I found someone to spend my life with, a vague fear about a new form of life also rushes in together.
