As I prepare the wedding invitations and look back at the past time, I realize anew that we have gone through a lot together. My body is tired because there are many things to take care of ahead of the wedding, but amidst that, I feel like we understand each other even more. Sometimes there are moments when I want to run away like this without preparation, but I decided to accept even such feelings as part of this process. On the wedding day, I definitely want to remember today's fluttering heart.
C1:그와 헤어지고 나서야 우리가 얼마나 오랫동안 서로를 위해 노력해 왔: Only after breaking up with him did I realize how long we had tried for each other. My heart ached the entire time we had our last conversation, but for each other, we had no choice but to go our separate ways now. Every time I found pictures we took together while packing my things, my heart felt like it was breaking. Still, only after crying all my tears out did I get a little breathing room. The common saying that a breakup is not the end but another beginning brings a little comfort today. Starting tomorrow, I will try to focus a bit more on taking care of myself.
C1:창밖으로 익숙한 풍경이 조금씩 낯선 풍경으로 바뀌는 사이, 이제 정: While the familiar scenery outside the window slowly changed into unfamiliar scenery, the thought that I am really leaving now hit me. It didn't feel real just when I was waving goodbye with my parents, but while the train picked up speed, I gradually realized the weight of parting. So many emotions passed by today to the extent that my face reflected in the window felt unfamiliar. Seeing the neighborhood where I spent over twenty years getting smaller, the tip of my nose tingled. It is scary, but the expectation of meeting a tougher me at the end of this journey arises together. When I arrive, I should first leave this moment as a photo.
C1:봄맞이 대청소를 하다가 상자 안에서 대학 시절 쓰던 물건들을 잔뜩: While doing spring cleaning, I found a bunch of things I used during my college days inside a box. I laughed thinking that the twenty-year-old me cherished these things so much. Taking them out one by one with a sense of joy lasted only a moment, and soon I felt at a loss as to how to organize all this luggage. Debating whether to throw them away or not, I finally decided to keep a few because I didn't want to completely erase myself from those days. I realized for the first time today that organizing things is actually a matter of saying goodbye to the me of those days. After finishing everything, my room became much lighter, but my heart instead became heavy.
C1:오늘로 또 한 살을 먹었다. 지난 일 년을 돌아보면 크게 성공한 일: I am a year older as of today. Looking back at the past year, there were no major successes, but I have lived each day faithfully in my own way. Instead of boasting about flashy achievements, the time I spent quietly pulling myself together seems to have made the me of today. While blowing out the candles, I didn't make a special wish, but just put in the feeling that I want to keep walking without shaking like now. Seeing that getting older isn't as scary as before, I guess I have matured a little bit. I wonder what kind of appearance I will have when I read this writing again next year today. This year too, I want to live like myself and a little bit stronger.
C1:이곳에 온 지 벌써 한 달이 지났다. 언어가 서투른 통에 간단한 심: It has already been a month since I came here. Because my language is clumsy, even a simple errand takes several times longer. Only after finishing my bank business alone for the first time did I realize that I am truly living here. Every night, there are days when I cannot sleep thinking of food I miss and my family, but I am gradually getting used to the rhythm of this place. Because every single unfamiliar expression and gesture feels fresh, each and every day comes to me as new. I still have a long way to go, but I believe this unfamiliarity will someday become familiarity.
C1:아버지가 다음 달이면 삼십 년 넘게 다니시던 회사를 떠나신다. 어릴: Next month, my father will leave the company where he has worked for over thirty years. When I was young, I couldn't even imagine that a day would come when my father would retire. Watching him prepare for his last commute, a myriad of emotions crossed my mind. For the first time, I thought that my father, who always looked reliable and unshakable, might actually have gone to work with heavy steps every day. When I cautiously asked what he would do in the future, he said he wanted to start the hobbies he had put off until now. I want to become a daughter who can cheer for my father's new beginning by his side.
C1:오늘 조카가 그림을 그리는 모습을 보다가 문득 어릴 적 화가가 되고: Today, watching my nephew draw a picture, I suddenly thought of myself wanting to become a painter when I was young. Back then, I thought that dream would naturally come true someday, but looking back, it was just pushed aside by reality and quietly forgotten. I was surprised myself by the fact that it has been more than ten years since I put down the brush. A single crooked picture drawn by my nephew shook my heart greatly today. I cautiously think about whether I can pick up the brush again even now. Even if I don't have grand talent, I just want to draw again for the sake of enjoyment.
C1:아침에 눈을 뗬을 때만 해도 여느 때처럼 마루가 꼬리를 흔들며 반겨: When I opened my eyes in the morning, I thought Maru would wag his tail and greet me as usual. The first morning without Maru was much quieter and more unfamiliar than I thought. I didn't expect the empty space of a being shared for fifteen years to be this big. Even while organizing his food bowl and leash, I cried several times. I realized for the first time today that sadness is not something to hold back by force, but a process of learning how to let it flow. I want to repay the longing by living without forgetting the love Maru left behind.
C1:오늘도 늦은 밤까지 휴대폰을 붙들고 있다가 문득 이런 밤이 벌써 몇: Today too, while holding my phone late into the night, I suddenly ended up counting how many years nights like this have been going on. Welcoming the new year, I made up my mind to really cut this habit this time. I decided to stay away from the screen and open a book starting one hour before going to sleep. My hands will itch and it will be hard for a few days, but I am also curious how much this small change will alter the quality of my life. Since I made up my mind anyway, I decided to pull my morning wakeup time forward a bit. Even if it turns into a three-day resolution, I'm going to try starting from tonight.
Today in class, I stammered on a simple sentence and my face turned red. Every time I make a mistake due to awkward pronunciation, a momentary sense of shame rushes in. However, thinking deeply about it, learning this language seems to be a process of learning how to express myself anew, beyond simply memorizing words. The me who speaks haltingly like a child feels unfamiliar, but at the same time, it feels fresh. Every day, I practice encouraging myself that it's okay not to be perfect. Hoping for the day when I can freely speak my thoughts in this language someday, I make a little progress today as well.
C1:오늘부터 다시 대학원 수업을 듣기 시작했다. 젊은 학생들 사이에 앉: Starting today, I began attending graduate school classes again. Sitting among young students, I sometimes felt out of place myself. However, as I started at a late age, I want to learn with a more desperate heart. Compared to going to school without any thoughts in my early twenties, every moment feels precious now. My physical strength is not what it used to be, but my goals have become clearer accordingly. Rather than worrying about a late start, I feel a great sense of gratitude that I can start even now.
C1:오늘 오랜만에 만난 친구에게서 승진 소식을 들었다. 진심으로 축하해: Today, I heard news of a promotion from a friend I met after a long time. While I wanted to congratulate them sincerely, a sense of bitterness welled up in me in a corner of my heart without me knowing. I couldn't help but feel ashamed of myself for feeling such a petty emotion. All the way back home, I kept asking myself what I am doing right now. However, thinking carefully, my friend's speed and my speed were not comparable subjects from the beginning. I should let go of this emotion today too and keep moving forward at my own pace.
C1:혼자 살기 시작한 지 이제 반년이 넘었다. 처음 독립했을 때 밤마다: It has now been over half a year since I started living alone. Unlike when I first lived independently and couldn't sleep at night due to loneliness, these days, time alone feels comfortable instead. Around the time I prepare and eat dinner and quietly read a book, I feel at ease thinking that I spent today safely and well. At first, even boiling a single pack of ramen was clumsy, but now I make fairly decent meals. The fact that I am learning how to take care of myself one by one makes me proud. I want to live while cherishing this small sense of independence in the future as well.
While organizing the attic, I found an old photo album that my mother had kept. Seeing pictures of myself around the time I was just taking my first steps made me laugh naturally. The memory of going to the playground holding dad's hand tightly on the day this picture was taken feels fresh. Seeing the faces of my young parents inside the photos made me realize how much time has passed. Each and every old and faded photo seemed to contain the warmth of that time just as it was. I want to keep this photo album well for a long time and show it to my child later too.
C1:병원에서 퇴원한 지 벌써 한 달이 지났다. 큰 수술을 겪어 보고서야: It has already been a month since I was discharged from the hospital. Only after experiencing major surgery did I realize how precious the daily life I took for granted until now was. Just being able to open my eyes in the morning and start the day normally makes me feel grateful. In the past, I easily got annoyed even at trivial things, but now I am learning how to let things go a bit more leisurely. It is as if I learned how to listen to my body's signals only after getting sick. I want to live the remaining life a little slower and more preciously.
C1:이혼한 지 반년이 지났다. 처음에는 실패한 사람이 된 것 같아 한동: It has been half a year since my divorce. At first, I couldn't lift my head for a while because I felt like a person who had failed. However, these days, I think that divorce was not a failure in life, but an opportunity to redefine a new me. I am gradually learning how to live entirely as myself, not as someone's wife. The unfamiliar freedom I am experiencing for the first time is scary, but there are also many moments that are exciting because of it. I believe that today's me has become a little tougher than yesterday's me.
C1:아이를 낳기 전까지는 부모의 사랑이 얼마나 큰 것인지 머리로만 이해: Until I had a child, I think I only understood with my head how great a parent's love is. Holding a baby crying all night, my body is tired, but my heart is strangely full. I am personally feeling the change these days where I think of another existence before myself. The old me considered my time and tastes more important than anything, but now a single smile of my child has become a greater joy than that. This change feels unfamiliar yet fascinating. I am a clumsy parent, but I want to grow little by little along with my child.
C1:책장을 정리하던 참에 오래된 책 사이에서 편지 한 통이 툭 떨어졌다: While organizing my bookshelf, a letter suddenly dropped out from between old books. It was a letter written by a friend from my college days, and I didn't even know things like this still remained. Reading the crooked handwriting, I remembered again what kinds of worries the me of those days carried. Just as I was wondering where and what that friend is doing now, I suddenly wanted to get in touch. I didn't know a single handwritten letter would summon such a big emotion. Lately, I've come to want to feel the warmth of handwritten letters that I had forgotten and lived without.
C1:몇 달을 고민한 끝에 오늘 팀장님께 퇴사 의사를 전했다. 안정된 월: After pondering for months, I expressed my intention to resign to our team leader today. Instead of giving up a steady salary, I decided to find a path that suits me, even if it is a little late. It's not that the career I've built up so far isn't a pity, but I decided to count this time as a preparation period for a new beginning. My steps leaving the office felt relieved while at the same time feeling unfamiliar. I don't know what kind of difficulties lie ahead, but I want to do my best so I don't regret today's decision. I feel like I've just turned the first page of a new chapter.
C1:오늘은 명절인데도 혼자 조용한 방 안에 앉아 있다. 아침엔 괜찮은가: Today is a holiday, but I am sitting alone inside a quiet room. I thought I was fine in the morning, but after seeing pictures of my family, longing rushes in. The city visible outside the window just moves in an unfamiliar way, no different from usual. A holiday alone felt sad at first, but as time passed, I found myself becoming rather calm. Eating simply prepared food and seeing my family's faces through a video call was a bit of comfort just with that. I hope that around this time next year, I can spend the holiday together with my family.
C1:오늘로 마흔이 되었다. 무엇이든 다 이룰 수 있을 것 같던 시절과는: I turned forty today. Unlike the days when I thought I could achieve anything, now I humbly accept the fact that there are more things in life that don't go the way you want. The impatient heart I had when I was young has now become a bit more relaxed. Rather than regretting goals I failed to achieve, I try to accept the path I've walked so far itself. Seeing unfamiliar wrinkles in the mirror doesn't fluster me as much as before, which makes me think I've matured a little bit. For the next ten years, I want to walk without impatience, at my own pace.
C1:오늘 마지막으로 기타를 케이스에 넣으며 이 취미를 잠시 접기로 결심: Today, while putting my guitar into its case for the last time, I decided to put this hobby aside for a while. It has been over ten years since I started playing the guitar, but I couldn't help admitting that these days it doesn't excite me as much as before. Instead of holding on by force, I decided to keep some distance and rethink what I truly want. Seeing my hand shaking slightly as I closed the case, it seems regret isn't totally absent. I believe the day will come when I naturally pick up the guitar again someday. Right now, I just want to accept this decision without regret.
C1:오늘 팀 프로젝트가 결국 무산되었다는 소식을 들었다. 지난 여섯 달: Today I heard the news that the team project ultimately fell through. Since it was work I poured my affection into, hanging onto it day and night for the past six months, my disappointment is beyond words. However, I think this experience won't just stop at a simple failure. What I learned in this process will definitely help in future work. The conversations and worries I shared with team members while staying up all night were valuable times that will ultimately remain as assets. The regret is big, but in the next challenge, I want to use today's experience as a stepping stone.
It seems that as the expected childbirth date gets closer, fear grows bigger than excitement. It feels like I still can't even take care of myself properly, so there is no way it feels real that I am responsible for a life. The more I read parenting books, the more the fact that I am full of things I don't know hits me. Still, it is true that every time I look at the baby's ultrasound picture, an indescribable affection rushes in. I cannot become a perfect parent, but the feeling that I want to become a parent who gives love with all my heart is clear. It's unavoidable that the days ahead are scary yet exciting at the same time.
C1:일기를 쓰지 않은 지도 벌써 오 년이 넘었다는 걸 오늘에서야 깨달았: I realized only today that it has been over five years since I stopped keeping a diary. My mind has been cluttered often these days, so I picked up a pen after a long time with the intention of organizing my thoughts again. The first few lines were awkward so I didn't know what to write, but as I wrote, emotions I had forgotten came to mind one by one. Transferring the inner feelings I couldn't say aloud into writing makes my mind feel much lighter. From now on, even if it's not a grand day, I have a mind to leave records little by little every day. I hope this determination of tonight doesn't fizzle out after a few days.
C1:오늘 지하철에서 무너지듯 눈물을 흘렸는데, 낯선 할머니께서 조용히: Today I cried as if collapsing on the subway, and an unfamiliar grandmother quietly handed me a handkerchief. I never thought I would receive this kind of comfort from someone I see for the first time. Just having her sit by my side without any special words was a huge strength. Through that short encounter, I came to believe again in the fact that the world is still full of warm people. I don't remember her name or face well, but only the warmth of that handkerchief seems like it will stay for a long time. Someday, I want to become that kind of existence to someone as well.
C1:오늘 우연히 그의 결혼 소식을 전해 들었다. 예전 같았으면 하루 종: Today I happened to hear the news of his marriage. In the past, my heart would have shaken all day long, but now I am surprisingly calm. Around two years after breaking up, I think we naturally came to accept that we are each living our own lives. Seeing that I genuinely wish him well, I cannot help but admit that I have healed a lot during that time. I used to think my past love was a failure, but now I accept it as just a chapter of my life. Today's calmness seems to be the greatest gift time has given me.
C1:오늘 드디어 첫 자취방으로 이삿짐을 옮겼다. 텅 빈 방을 혼자 채워: Today I finally moved my luggage into my first solo room. Trying to fill the empty room alone feels daunting yet strangely exciting. From changing a light bulb to how to use the washing machine, I had to learn trivial things one by one anew. Trying to fix a single dinner meal myself without my parents, I laughed because I was clumsier than I thought. Still, organizing my luggage one by one in the small room, I could feel this place gradually becoming my own space. Clumsy as it is, I believe this unfamiliar independence will make me tougher.
C1:오늘 십 년 만에 고등학교 은사님을 찾아뵈었다. 이렇게 오랜 세월이: Today I visited my high school teacher after ten years. I didn't expect the teacher to recognize me at a glance even after such a long time. His kindly smiling appearance was just like back then, so my heart felt moved for some reason. The consideration and affection of the teacher that I didn't know in the past are felt a bit more deeply now. It was a short meeting, but I could recall the grateful feelings I had been living without forgetting. I vowed to visit him again next time before it's too late.
C1:낯선 도시의 시장을 혼자 정처 없이 돌아다니다가 문득 걸음을 멈췄다: Wandering aimlessly alone through the market of an unfamiliar city, I suddenly stopped walking. Seeing myself enjoying the day comfortably even without a plan like this, I was surprised myself. Ordinarily, I was always a person who felt at ease only when moving according to a schedule, but here, that side of me was loosening up little by little. I never imagined I would stay so long at a single scenery I happened to meet in an unfamiliar alley. Stepping out of my familiar frame, I learned that there was a relaxed mindset I didn't know I had inside me. Even after this trip ends, I want to keep this unfamiliar relaxation without forgetting it.
C1:새해 첫날, 조용히 앉아 지난 한 해를 돌아보았다. 그동안 남들이: On the first day of the new year, I sat quietly and looked back at the past year. I asked myself whether I had just lived being pushed along to the speed set by others. I felt a bit bitter because it seemed like I had just consumed each day without a clear goal. So, taking the first day of the new year as an opportunity, I decided to sort out what I really want again this year. Rather than grand goals, I want to make a year where I am honest with myself. I hope that around the time this year ends, I can say it was a year without regrets.
C1:몇 년째 서로 말도 섞지 않을 정도로 서먹했던 언니와 오늘 오랜만에: Today, I sat across from my older sister for the first time in a long time, after being so awkward with each other for years that we didn't even speak. You have no idea how many nights I hesitated before finally offering an apology first. Opening up my heart with difficulty, I finally learned that the misunderstandings that had piled up during that time were actually very small things. Seeing us wipe away tears and smile, I realized anew how much we missed each other during that time. I realized that feelings we took for granted just because we are family are ultimately not conveyed if we don't express them. I want to keep today's reconciliation precious in the future as well.
C1:오늘은 여러모로 내 인생의 전환점이 되는 날이다. 앞으로의 길이 순: Today is a turning point in my life in many ways. Even if the path ahead is not smooth, I want to walk this direction I chose myself without regrets. Until now, I have only picked safe choices, but now I vow to move toward what I truly want, even if it's a little scary. Even if I fail, it will be a much more valuable experience than not even trying. Even if moments of shaking come, I will try not to forget today's determination. I hope that when I look back at today a few years later, it is a choice I am not ashamed of.
C1:전세란 세입자가 매달 월세를 내는 대신 집값의 상당 부분에 해당하는: Jeonse is a rental method in which the tenant leaves a deposit equivalent to a significant portion of the house price to the landlord instead of paying monthly rent, and resides there during the contract period. The landlord can make a profit by operating this deposit, while the tenant has the advantage of significantly reducing the burden of monthly housing expenses. When the contract ends, the deposit is in principle refunded in full, but recently, concerns about so-called 'jeonse fraud' are growing due to this. If housing prices fall, the so-called 'empty jeonse' problem occurs where landlords cannot return the deposit. Because of this, the government has continued to push for institutional improvements, such as making subscription to jeonse deposit guarantee insurance mandatory. The jeonse system symbolizes Korea's unique housing culture, but at the same time, it has consistently been the subject of debate due to its risks.
C1:회식은 업무 시간이 끝난 뒤 부서원들이 함께 식사와 술자리를 갖는: A company dinner is an occasion where department members have meals and drinks together after work hours, and on the surface, its purpose is to build camaraderie. While Western company dinner cultures generally presuppose voluntary participation, Korean company dinners have long taken on a semi-forced character. Unlike the past when attendance was taken for granted regardless of rank, recently an atmosphere respecting individual choices has taken root. There is definitely a positive aspect that at company dinners, you can comfortably share stories that are usually difficult to tell. However, excessive coercion to drink and late homecoming times are still pointed out as areas needing improvement. Ultimately, company dinners can be said to be a practice with dual aspects of strengthening organizational solidarity while potentially infringing upon individual lives.
C1:긱 이코노미란 정규직 고용 대신 필요할 때마다 단기 계약으로 노동력: The gig economy refers to an economic form where labor is bought and sold through short-term contracts whenever needed instead of regular employment. As delivery agencies or car-sharing platforms spread, this form of labor is increasing rapidly. Workers enjoy the advantage of being able to work freely at desired times, but in reality, there is almost no job stability. Because they do not belong to a company, there are many cases where it is difficult to receive basic protections such as the four major public insurances or severance pay. As the influence of platform companies grows, the problem of power imbalance between workers and companies is also coming to the spotlight. Ultimately, the gig economy has expanded labor flexibility, but behind it lies only an unstable life.
C1:도시 재생이란 낡고 쇠퇴한 지역을 완전히 철거하는 대신 기존의 골격: Urban regeneration is an urban development method that newly reorganizes old and declined areas while keeping their existing frameworks, instead of completely demolishing them. Before proceeding with regeneration projects, the process of sufficiently gathering the opinions of local residents must precede. The method of remodeling old buildings to turn them into workshops or cafes while preserving the original shape of alleys as much as possible is often utilized. This method receives positive evaluations in that it breathes new vitality while protecting the identity of the region. However, the more successful regeneration is, the more gentrification problems follow where rents soar and original residents are rather pushed out. Therefore, urban regeneration is a task that must consider not only the improvement of the physical environment but also the social balance to protect the existing community.
C1:한국은 전 세계에서 유례없이 빠른 속도로 고령화가 진행되고 있는 국: Korea is counted as a country where aging is progressing at an unprecedentedly fast speed in the world. The biggest problem pointed out is that while the proportion of the elderly population continues to increase, the working-age population to support them is rather decreasing. As life expectancy increases, the financial burden placed on social security systems such as the national pension and health insurance is also growing. A reversal phenomenon is appearing where the youth generation's population is decreasing due to low birth rates, while the elderly group's size is growing day by day. In small rural towns, as this aging speed becomes even faster, the number of places facing the crisis of the village itself disappearing is increasing. Ultimately, the aging problem can be said to be not just a change in demographic statistics, but a task testing the sustainability of the entire nation.
C1:한국의 아파트 단지는 여러 동의 건물이 하나의 울타리 안에 모여 있: An apartment complex in Korea is a large-scale housing form where multiple buildings gather within a single fence, and it is like forming a small village beyond a simple living space. Inside the complex, not only playgrounds and exercise facilities but also living convenience facilities such as senior centers and daycare centers are often equipped together. Residents share management fees to receive services such as security, cleaning, and facility maintenance, and they also directly participate in complex management through the residents' representative meeting. Most complexes have underground parking lots, so they are created as pedestrian-centered spaces where vehicles do not run on the ground. Complexes with good school districts and transportation themselves become the standard that dictates local real estate prices. Like this, apartment complexes can be said to be a representative housing form that simultaneously reflects Korean daily life and asset-forming methods.
C1:협동조합은 이윤 극대화를 목표로 하는 일반 기업과 달리 조합원들의: Unlike general companies aiming for profit maximization, cooperatives are economic organizations that prioritize the common interests of their members. Members pay investment funds to become the owners of the cooperative and at the same time have the right to participate in management with equal qualifications. In general stock companies, the more shares one has, the greater the voice becomes, whereas cooperatives follow the principle of one vote per member regardless of shares. This structure can be said to be a device to prevent a minority of capital from controlling the organization. When profits are generated, they are distributed to members, while some are reinvested in projects for the local community. However, as the decision-making process is democratic, the limitation that prompt decisions are difficult also naturally reveals itself.
C1:재택근무가 보편화되면서 사무실에서는 불필요했던 새로운 형태의 업무: As working from home has become common, a new form of business etiquette that was unnecessary in the office has begun to take root naturally. In video conferences, connecting accurately at the designated time is considered basic etiquette, while the perception that one must pay some attention to background or clothing is spreading. Since people cannot see each other in person, the tone of messages is bound to feel stiffer than in reality, so cases of adding emoticons or soft expressions have increased. Contacting after work hours is accepted as a discourtesy, while a culture of not expecting immediate responses is also being formed together. On the other hand, because the other person's situation cannot be visually checked, misunderstandings are easily bound to occur. Ultimately, work-from-home etiquette can be said to stem from efforts to bridge physical distance with psychological consideration.
C1:과거 세대는 결혼을 성인이 되면 당연히 거쳐야 할 절차로 여기는 데: While past generations regarded marriage as a natural procedure to go through when becoming an adult, recent young generations tend to accept marriage as one of several options. It can be seen that while the older generation views marriage and childbirth as the completion of a stable life, the younger generation considers economic burdens and individual freedom as more important values. In particular, many views consider the rise in housing and child-rearing costs as realistic factors that make people delay or give up marriage. As women's advancement into society becomes active, the number of people who view that the past formula where marriage means stability is no longer valid is increasing. This change should be viewed not as a simple generational conflict, but as the result of changes in the entire social structure. Ultimately, differences in views on marriage can be said to reflect differences in the economic and social environments each generation faces.
C1:한국의 편의점은 24시간 운영되는 소매점을 넘어 도시 생활 곳곳에: Convenience stores in Korea go beyond retail stores operating 24 hours to act as social infrastructure permeating every corner of urban life. Not only can simple meals and daily necessities be purchased late at night, but administrative conveniences such as paying various utility bills or dropping off courier services are also provided together. Most convenience stores are equipped with cash dispensers and eating spaces where people can sit and eat, thereby acting as small living bases. As single-person households increase, the demand for convenience stores where small-packaged products can be purchased without burden continues to increase. When disasters or emergencies occur, they are utilized as bases for temporarily distributing relief goods and also play the role of safety monitoring networks for local residents. Like this, convenience stores have gone beyond simple commercial facilities to settle as essential spaces sustaining the daily lives of urbanites.
C1:설날과 추석이 되면 수많은 사람들이 고향을 찾아 이동하는 귀성 행렬: When Seollal and Chuseok arrive, a homecoming procession of numerous people moving to visit their hometowns continues nationwide. This is an occasion where family members who lived scattered gather in one place to share regards, and at the same time, it is an opportunity to continue traditions by holding ancestral rites for ancestors. While many people use the holidays as an opportunity to meet relatives after a long time and re-establish relationships, quite a few people feel a burden from holiday labor and nagging. In particular, holiday housework concentrated on women has long been a social controversy. Recently, taking this as an opportunity, the number of households replacing holidays with simplified ancestral rites or travel is also on the rise. Like this, homecoming customs preserve the traditions of the family community while their forms are gradually changing according to the changes of the times.
C1:구독 경제란 상품이나 서비스를 소유하는 대신 일정 금액을 정기적으로: The subscription economy refers to a consumption method where people pay a fixed amount regularly and use products or services instead of owning them. Started in video streaming or music services, this method is now applied to automobiles, furniture, and even groceries, thereby changing the very concept of consumption. Consumers can use desired services without spending a large sum of money, but if they maintain multiple subscriptions simultaneously, expenditures only accumulate without notice. From the company's perspective, the ability to continuously secure stable profits acts as the biggest attraction. As the number of subscription services increases, users often fail to even grasp which services they use and how much. Ultimately, the subscription economy is not free from criticism that while it provides the convenience of consumption, it merely instigates unconscious spending.
C1:한국의 배달 문화를 이해하기에 앞서 이 나라의 높은 인구 밀도와 빠: Before understanding Korea's delivery culture, it is necessary to examine this country's high population density and fast delivery infrastructure first. Most downtown areas are equipped with dense road networks and motorcycle delivery networks, so it is common to receive food within thirty years—correction, thirty minutes after ordering. Delivery apps handle not only food but also daily necessities and medicines, and they also provide a function to check the delivery person's location in real-time. Before using these services, consumers have acquired consumption habits of carefully comparing reviews and ratings. In conjunction with the increase in single-person households, the demand for delivery food is steadily increasing, and the scale of the related market is also continuing to grow. However, behind it, the shadow of the poor working environment of delivery workers also exists together.
C1:한국의 공교육 과정은 표준화된 교육 과정을 제공하는 데 반해 대학: Korea's public education course provides a standardized curriculum, whereas college entrance exams have an extremely fierce competitive structure, so private education demand to bridge that gap continuously occurs. As the perception that entering prestigious universities has a big impact on subsequent employment and income levels strengthens, parents show a tendency to invest heavily in their children's education. While public education provides average classes targeting the majority, academies are differentiated in that they provide customized classes tailored to individual levels. As the scale of the private education market grows, the influence that a household's economic conditions exert on children's academic achievement is also growing together. Consequently, this produces a vicious cycle where educational gaps lead to income gaps, and income gaps lead back to educational gaps. Even though the government has released private education suppression policies several times, it has not reaped great effects due to these structural factors.
C1:지역 축제는 특산물이나 역사적 배경 등 지역만의 고유한 자원을 알리: Local festivals are events led by local governments to promote unique local resources such as local specialties or historical backgrounds. A successful festival becomes an occasion to increase visits by outsiders while also bringing actual sales increases to local commercial districts. It is not rare that through festivals, regions that were usually not well-known receive nationwide attention. During the festival period, local residents earn extra income by selling local specialties or operating experience programs, while also feeling pride in their region. However, some festivals lack differentiation in content and are criticized as a waste of budget. Ultimately, local festivals can be seen to act as an occasion to revitalize the local economy while simultaneously reaffirming local identity.
C1:제3의 공간이란 집과 직장이 아닌, 개인이 자유롭게 머물며 쉴 수: The third space is a concept referring to a space where individuals can freely stay and rest, other than home and work. Today, cafes can be seen to function not simply as places to drink beverages, but as multipurpose spaces to work or meet people. In particular, many views consider that the fact that people can concentrate in a wide and pleasant environment away from narrow living spaces leads many people to cafes. Cafes equipped with wireless internet and power outlets now play the role of a kind of temporary office and are also widely utilized as study group or small meeting venues. As urbanization progresses, some experts view that the narrowing of individuals' private spaces is the background for the spread of cafe culture. Like this, cafes have settled as spaces that simultaneously provide modern urbanites with psychological rest and social exchange.
C1:한국 사회에서는 대학의 이름 자체가 개인의 능력을 평가하는 주요 기: In Korean society, the tendency for the name of the university itself to act as a major criterion for evaluating an individual's ability has continued for a long time. While a small number of prestigious universities enjoy substantial advantages in employment and social status, the remaining universities are rarely narrowing that gap. There is an analysis that this hierarchical structure originated from the historical background of having to rapidly foster a small number of talents during the industrialization period. Since the brand value is prioritized over the practical educational content of universities, students merely try to enter top-tier universities even while enduring retaking the exam or partial attendance. Although the government and universities have attempted to ease the hierarchy several times, deep-rooted perceptions only fail to change easily. Ultimately, this culture can be said to reveal the limitation of evaluating an individual's various potentials with a single yardstick.
C1:최저임금이 꾸준히 인상됨에 따라 인건비 부담을 줄이기 위해 무인 매: As the minimum wage is steadily raised, self-employed people introducing unmanned stores to reduce labor cost burdens are increasing. While spreading first in relatively simple businesses like unmanned ice cream shops or unmanned laundromats, recently it is also being tried in complex businesses like convenience stores and cafes. By cutting labor costs, operators can improve profitability, but store management and theft prevention must rely entirely on systems. While existing stores operate on the premise of face-to-face communication with employees, unmanned stores are thoroughly premised on autonomous payment and use. As technology develops, automated payment systems using AI cameras are also being gradually introduced. These changes provide convenience while simultaneously leaving behind the social task of job reduction.
C1:1인 가구가 늘어나면서 정서적 유대를 나눌 대상으로 반려동물을 선택: As single-person households increase, people choosing pets as targets to share emotional bonds with are rapidly increasing. As the population raising pets grows, the scale of related industries also grows together, forming a single huge market. Not only are pet-only cafes and hospitals increasing, but accommodations and restaurants where pets can accompany are also greatly increasing. This change shows the recognition change of treating pets not as mere objects of affection, but as family members. However, without fully considering the responsibilities and costs accompanying pet raising, the number of abandoned animals is also increasing together. Ultimately, the spread of pet culture is a positive change that raises the quality of life while simultaneously being an occasion demanding new social responsibilities.
C1:온라인 커뮤니티는 비슷한 관심사를 가진 사람들이 모여 정보를 교환하: Online communities have grown into spaces where people with similar interests gather to exchange information and share opinions. While such spaces become passages where even minority voices can be freely expressed, they also produce side effects where specific public opinions are excessively amplified. Experts view that when homogeneous members inside communities exchange opinions, biased perspectives easily become even more reinforced. There are also views that because information is often rapidly spread without verifying its factual accuracy, it can become a hotbed of fake news. Nevertheless, communities perform the positive function of publicizing issues that existing media do not cover, while also playing the role of representing the voices of social minorities. Ultimately, online communities have settled as a new axis of public opinion formation, but responsible use is required as much as their influence.
C1:프랜차이즈란 본사가 개발한 브랜드와 운영 시스템을 가맹점주가 일정한: A franchise refers to a business form where a store owner uses a brand and operational system developed by the headquarters by paying a certain cost. Before concluding a franchise contract, prospective founders must thoroughly check the headquarters' financial status and the performance of existing stores. The headquarters provides brand awareness and verified operational know-how, but merely receives royalties every month in return. If someone borrows excessively, trusting only expected sales before starting a business, it can become a great burden on management. Even if a new store of the same brand opens nearby with overlapping commercial districts, store owners often just have to endure this as it is. Ultimately, franchise businesses can be said to be a structure where guaranteed stability is received in exchange for significantly restricted autonomous management rights.
C1:한국의 재활용 분리배출 제도는 쓰레기를 종이, 플라스틱, 유리, 금: Korea's recycling separation disposal system stipulates that garbage must be subdivided and discharged into paper, plastics, glass, metals, etc. While other countries apply relatively simple classification systems, Korea is equipped with an elaborate system that even requires food waste to be discharged separately. As separation disposal is properly carried out, there are effects of increasing the recovery rate of recyclable resources and reducing disposal costs. In apartment complexes, items that can be discharged are designated by day of the week, whereas in single-family housing areas, regulations are often applied relatively loosely. As environmental awareness rises, a system for separately discharging transparent plastic bottles has even been newly introduced recently. Although there are complaints that this subdivided system is cumbersome, it substantially contributes to raising the resource recycling rate.
C1:한국의 직장 문화에서는 오랫동안 정시에 퇴근하는 것이 성실하지 못한: In Korean workplace culture, there was for a long time a strong atmosphere where leaving work on time was considered an insincere attitude. While subordinates remained behind, reading the room if the boss kept their seat, a practice of staying late regardless of actual workload took root. Under this culture, people who kept their seats long rather than those who finished work efficiently were bound to receive better evaluations. However, since the introduction of the 52-hour workweek system, perceptions of overtime have been gradually changing, while overtime itself has begun to be legally restricted. As voices wanting to respect personal time grow centered around the younger generation, the atmosphere that took overtime for granted is naturally weakening. Ultimately, the change in overtime culture can be said to be an indicator showing that the entire society's values regarding labor are changing.
C1:한국에서는 처음 만나는 사람과 인사를 나눌 때 두 손으로 명함을 주: In Korea, exchanging business cards with both hands when greeting someone you meet for the first time has settled as general etiquette. Business cards specify not only names and titles but also affiliated companies and departments, so they can be seen to act as a means to immediately grasp the other person's social position. Starting from this short exchange, forms of address, speech styles, and even conversational attitudes between two people are often naturally decided. Experts view that this practice reflects Korea's unique organizational culture that values hierarchy and ranks. Since a first impression of the other person is formed through the short moment of exchanging business cards, the number of people paying attention to business card designs is increasing. Like this, although it is merely a small piece of paper, Korea's hierarchical culture can be seen to be intactly contained behind it.
C1:배달 앱은 소상공인에게 별도의 홍보 없이도 많은 잠재 고객에게 노출: Delivery apps provide small business owners with the opportunity to be exposed to many potential customers without separate promotion. While large franchises have the capacity to build their own delivery networks, small self-employed business owners have no choice but to have a much higher dependency on delivery apps. Using delivery apps has the advantage of not only increasing sales but also securing new customer groups that did not visit the store. However, as orders increase, the burden of brokerage fees and delivery costs also grows together, so actual net profits often do not increase much. Considering even advertising expenses to raise the exposure ranking on delivery apps, the burden on self-employed people not only worsens further, but sales also fluctuate greatly depending on app policy changes. Ultimately, delivery apps can be said to have opened new sales channels for small business owners while simultaneously creating another form of subjugation.
C1:공유 오피스란 여러 개인이나 기업이 하나의 사무 공간을 나누어 사용: A shared office refers to a work space where multiple individuals or companies share a single office space and use meeting rooms and office equipment together. As startups and freelancers increase, the demand to use spaces only as much as needed rather than renting separate offices is growing. Initial founders prefer shared offices in many cases because they can greatly reduce fixed costs while obtaining a professional work environment. As remote work spreads, cases of large company employees utilizing shared offices near their homes like satellite offices are increasing. Since people from various industries gather in one space, it is also naturally an occasion to obtain networking opportunities. Like this, shared offices can be said to be a new work space model grown by the intertwined demands of cost reduction and flexibility.
C1:한국에서는 명절 연휴가 끝난 직후 이혼 상담과 신청 건수가 눈에 띄: In Korea, the phenomenon where divorce counseling and application cases noticeably increase immediately after holiday periods ends is repeated every year. Holidays when the whole family gathers in one place after a long time often become occasions where conflicts between couples and between mothers-in-law and daughters-in-law are surfaced. Holiday labor and guest hospitality lasting for several days make people revisit the issue of role division between couples, while also acting as an occasion to burst out frustrations that have been suppressed meanwhile. In particular, housework burdens concentrated on women have long been pointed out as core causes of marital conflict. Stress accumulated during holidays acts as an occasion for serious conversation after the holiday ends, while also acting as a decisive moment to reconsider relationships. This phenomenon can be said to be a stark example showing that the traditional event called holidays is colliding with modern family structures.
C1:한국의 대중목욕탕은 단순히 몸을 씻는 공간을 넘어 지역 주민들이 자: Korea's public bathhouses have long played the role of social spaces where local residents naturally interact, going beyond spaces to simply wash bodies. Here, people can comfortably converse with neighbors, and it also becomes a field to exchange information and wisdom transcending generations. While Western public bathing culture values individual privacy, Korea's bathhouses consider the very act of undressing and washing together as a means to form intimacy. As they developed into jjimjilbangs, they expanded into complex cultural spaces where people can enjoy not only bathing but also sleeping and entertainment. While the younger generation prefers private spaces, middle-aged and older generations still often regard meetings in bathhouses as a natural part of daily life. Like this, bathhouse culture is accepted differently depending on the generation, but it still remains as a symbolic space showing Koreans' community spirit.
C1:1인 가구가 전체 가구 형태 중 가장 큰 비중을 차지하게 됨에 따라: As single-person households come to occupy the largest proportion among all household forms, the center of gravity of the consumer market is also moving rapidly. Instead of large-capacity products centered on large supermarkets, demand for foods and daily necessities packaged in small quantities is increasing, and the single-person home appliance market is also growing greatly. As people living alone increase, products that shorten the cooking process like meal kits or semi-cooked foods are also receiving the spotlight. Delivery services can be used without burden even for small orders, and restaurants with single seats for people eating alone are also on the rise. As consumption related to pets and hobbies increases, consumer trends seeking to satisfy emotional fulfillment are also standing out together. These changes show that changes in Korean society's family structures are having a direct impact on the overall consumer market.
C1:인턴십은 정식 채용에 앞서 짧은 기간 동안 실무를 경험해 볼 수 있: Internships are a system where people can experience practical work for a short period before official hiring, and many companies operate them as part of new-hire recruitment procedures. While some companies actively utilize internship experiences as stepping stones for conversion to regular employment, other companies use them only as a means to secure low-cost labor. Interns can gain practical experience and careers to write on resumes, but the actual possibility of conversion to regular employment is often low, so it falls short of expectations. While there are interns who are deeply put into actual work, there are not a few cases where interns finish their internships after only taking charge of simple repetitive tasks. This imbalance ultimately leads to criticism that it has merely added another employment barrier for young job seekers. Nevertheless, internships still hold significance in that they are opportunities to learn practical senses and experience organizational culture in advance.
C1:청약 제도는 새로 지어지는 아파트를 분양받고자 하는 사람들이 신청하: The subscription system is a procedure where people wishing to be allocated newly built apartments apply, and winners are sorted by scoring based on the period of non-homeownership and the number of dependents. Before applying for a subscription, applicants must thoroughly check qualification requirements according to the region they reside in and their non-homeownership status. The recent reality is that the more popular the region is, the more competition surges, so winning probabilities are gradually getting lower. The longer one has subscribed to a subscription savings account and the longer the non-homeownership period is, the higher the plus points become, and the possibility of winning also grows together. If you do not make fund plans before proceeding with the contract, you may experience difficulties in the intermediate payment loan process. This system was prepared with the intent to provide opportunities to own a home for actual homeless demanders, but in reality, winning itself is becoming a very difficult gateway.
C1:프리랜서는 특정 회사에 소속되지 않고 여러 의뢰인과 계약을 맺어 일: Freelancers refer to a labor form where people work by signing contracts with various clients without belonging to a specific company. While freelancers enjoy the freedom to decide their working hours and locations by themselves, they must also endure the instability that their income is not constant. Experts view that the development of digital platforms accelerated the spread of the labor form called freelancers. Unlike regular employees, freelancers receive almost no institutional protections such as the four major public insurances or paid leave, while tax reporting and management must be resolved by themselves. To resolve these blind spots, some experts view that a separate social security system for freelancers is necessary. Ultimately, the labor form called freelancers can be said to be a double-edged sword possessing both the advantage of autonomy and the disadvantage of instability.
C1:노키즈존이란 안전사고나 소음 문제를 이유로 어린이 동반 입장을 제한: No-kids zones refer to restaurants or cafes that restrict the entry of accompanied children for reasons of safety accidents or noise problems. Business operators running such establishments argue that they can prevent children's safety accidents and also reduce inconveniences for other customers. Opposing viewpoints view that such policies are not only clear discrimination against children but also infringe upon parents' legitimate outing rights. In fact, some parents reveal that they feel it is discriminatory to have experienced entry refusal solely for the reason of being accompanied by a child. Business operators view that instead of taking issue with specific customers' behaviors, the method of excluding all children is rather more convenient. This debate can be said to be a representative example where the two values of private business owners' business freedom and the guarantee of children's rights collide.
C1:한국은 인구 대비 명품 소비 규모가 세계적으로도 손꼽힐 만큼 명품에: Korea is known as a country where interest in luxury goods is so passionate that it ranks among the top globally in terms of luxury consumption relative to population. In the past, luxury goods were regarded as the exclusive property of the middle-aged and older generations, whereas recently, luxury consumption by people in their twenties and thirties is noticeably increasing. An analysis comes out that triggered by the spread of the culture of showing off one's consumption through social media, luxury purchases have settled as a single self-expression method. While the desire to reveal one's social status through expensive objects has existed from before, it has been further strengthened by meeting a new passage called social media. Triggered by the phenomenon of even braving open runs to purchase luxury goods, voices of concern regarding conspicuous consumption are also growing together. Ultimately, the luxury consumption craze can be seen as a phenomenon reflecting the desire for social recognition beyond individual tastes.
C1:한국의 주거 형태 대부분을 차지하는 아파트는 구조상 위아래 층 간의: Apartments, which occupy most of Korea's housing forms, are bound by their structure to have noises between upper and lower floors transmitted as they are. Minor living noises like footsteps or dragging furniture, if repeated, are bound to spread into conflicts between neighbors, and cases leading to actual serious fights are not few. Inter-floor noise goes beyond simple inconvenience to destroy trust between neighbors and in extreme cases even flare up into violent incidents. When you go directly to protest to solve the problem, it is bound to flare up into an emotional fight instead, so mediation through the management office is recommended. Recently, institutional solutions such as the introduction of noise-reduction mats or inter-floor noise management committees are being prepared, and floor standards for newly built apartments are also being strengthened. Nevertheless, inter-floor noise remains a structural problem that is difficult to completely resolve as long as communal housing forms are maintained.
C1:정부가 창업 지원 정책을 확대하고 벤처 투자 시장이 성장함에 따라: As the government expanded startup support policies and the venture investment market grew, Korea's startup ecosystem has also rapidly grown in size. Centered around Pangyo and Gangnam districts, information technology startups are clustered, while startup fever based on region-specific industries is also spreading in local areas. As government support funds and private investments flow in together, the threshold for securing initial startup funds has also become lower than before. While cases of successful startups growing into unicorn companies are increasing, pointers that support systems for failed startups to rechallenge are still lacking are also raised. As cases of talents from large corporations moving to startups increase, the flows of organizational culture and talent influx are also changing together. While this growth is evaluated as a positive signal, concerns over excessive investment concentration are also raised together.
C1:대형마트 의무휴업 제도는 대형 유통업체의 시장 잠식으로 인해 위기에: The large supermarket mandatory closing system was introduced to protect traditional markets and alley commercial districts facing crises due to large distribution companies' market encroachment. Triggered by the past practice where large supermarkets operated without resting even on Sundays, self-employed people's backlash grew, and this system began to be discussed in earnest. While traditional market merchants evaluate that this system helps in actual sales recovery, consumers also raise complaints that grocery shopping has become inconvenient. Some studies have produced results that consumers shifted their consumption to online shopping instead of traditional markets on mandatory closing days. Large supermarket workers evaluate positively that they have come to be guaranteed rest rights triggered by mandatory holidays, while the distribution industry worries about sales losses and demands system easing. Like this, this system remains a representative policy controversy where the purpose of protecting traditional commercial districts and the value of consumer convenience fiercely confront each other.
C1:재건축은 낡은 아파트를 완전히 철거하고 새로 짓는 사업을, 재개발은: Reconstruction refers to a project to completely demolish old apartments and build new ones, and redevelopment refers to a project to reorganize entire aging residential areas. Before pushing forward with projects, residents must go through procedures of forming associations and passing safety diagnoses. When reconstruction is completed, existing residents not only gain the right to move into new apartments but can also expect rises in asset values. However, before entering into construction, cases where projects are delayed due to disagreements among association members and conflicts surrounding the selection of construction companies are not few. If projects become prolonged, residents must not only endure economic burdens following moving and temporary residence, but also experience the sense of loss of having to leave their beloved neighborhoods. Like this, reconstruction and redevelopment have effects of improving the living environment, but various social costs occur together in the process.
C1:설날과 추석이 되면 가족과 지인, 거래처에 선물을 주고받는 것이 오: When Seollal and Chuseok arrive, giving and receiving gifts to family, acquaintances, and business partners has settled as an old holiday custom. In the past, practical daily necessities like sesame oil or sugar were main gifts, whereas recently, gifts respecting tastes like health functional foods or gift certificates are gaining popularity. As consumers' selection ranges widen, department stores and online shopping malls are competitively presenting holiday gift sets in various price ranges. While some companies still send expensive gifts to business partners, a trend of lowering gift price ranges under the influence of the Improper Solicitation Act is also appearing recently. As single-person households increase, demand for small-packaged, small-capacity gift sets is also increasing together. Like this, the holiday gift culture continues to change its appearance in pace with changing consumer trends of the times and social system changes.
C1:결혼 정보 회사는 회원들의 학력, 직업, 자산 등의 정보를 바탕으로: Marriage information companies provide services introducing matched partners based on members' information such as educational background, occupation, and assets. Users often use these services because they view that it is difficult to obtain natural meeting opportunities amidst busy daily lives. Companies classify members' information by grade and even provide after-services after meetings to induce successful marriages. Some reveal critical perspectives, viewing that this method quantifies people by conditions. On the other hand, others view that it is a rational method to efficiently explore partners ahead of the weighty decision called marriage. Despite limitations such as considerably high usage costs and no guarantee of successful marriages, demand for marriage information companies continues steadily.
C1:나는 전 국민 기본소득 도입에 찬성하는 입장이다. 자동화로 일자리가: I am in favor of introducing a universal basic income for all citizens. In a situation where jobs are rapidly decreasing due to automation, a basic income can serve as a safety net that guarantees a minimum livelihood. While concerns are raised that it could dampen the willingness to work, some studies show that it actually gives people the leeway to escape low-wage precarious labor and find jobs that suit them. Of course, it cannot be denied that massive financing is required, and this is a task that is difficult to realize without tax reform. Nevertheless, I believe that in an era where inequality is deepening, such redistribution policies will contribute to social integration. Ultimately, I think that a basic income is worth pursuing cautiously, on the premise of discussing specific plans for raising financial resources together.
C1:나는 공공장소에서의 감시 카메라 확대가 제한적으로는 필요하다고 생각: I think that the expansion of surveillance cameras in public places is necessary on a limited basis. In areas with high crime rates, statistics show that the incidence of incidents has actually decreased after the installation of cameras. However, as surveillance is strengthened, citizens' privacy is increasingly shrinking, while its effectiveness is not always clearly proven. In particular, when combined with facial recognition technology, one cannot help but worry about the risk that governments or corporations will excessively track individuals' movements. Therefore, rather than opposing the installation of cameras itself, I believe that institutional devices that strictly restrict the storage period and access rights of video data should precede it. I think safety and freedom are not a matter of choosing one, but a matter of finding a balance.
C1:나는 인공지능이 단독으로 생성한 작품에 인간 창작물과 동등한 저작권: I think we should be cautious about granting copyright equal to human creations to works generated solely by artificial intelligence. The copyright system was originally designed to protect the efforts and intentions of creators, and it is difficult to see artificial intelligence as having such subjective intentions. I think it is timely that this issue has begun to be actively discussed following the recent spread of generative artificial intelligence. Of course, not recognizing copyright even for works completed by utilizing artificial intelligence as a tool may excessively reduce the rights of creators. Therefore, I believe that whether or not to recognize rights should be judged based on the degree to which humans substantially intervened in the creative process. As technology develops, the task of refining these criteria will definitely be necessary.
C1:나는 인구 감소와 노동력 부족 문제를 겪는 사회일수록 이민자 수용을: I think that societies experiencing population decline and labor shortages need to expand the acceptance of immigrants. Giving opportunities to people who want to work diligently regardless of nationality brings positive effects to the economy as a whole. In fact, looking at the cases of various immigrant countries, the influx of immigrants has simultaneously boosted industrial diversity and innovation. However, the concerns of existing residents about cultural conflict and job competition are also fully understandable. To resolve these concerns, beyond simply opening the door, language education and social integration programs must be prepared together. Ultimately, I believe that the success or failure of immigration policy depends on the quality of the integration process rather than the scale of acceptance.
C1:나는 도시 확장보다 고밀도 개발을 우선해야 한다고 생각한다. 도시가: I think high-density development should be prioritized over urban expansion. When cities spread indiscriminately to the outskirts, not only is the natural ecosystem encroached upon, but the efficiency of public transportation also drops significantly. Before developing new sites, adjusting the floor area ratio of the existing downtown is more rational in terms of resource utilization. Of course, it cannot be ignored that problems such as infringement of sunlight and view rights follow when high-rise buildings are crowded. However, since this goes beyond ruining the urban aesthetic and actually determines the quality of life of residents, I believe it can be supplemented with careful design standards. Ultimately, to create a sustainable city, I think compressed and dense development is a better direction than indiscriminate expansion.
C1:나는 온라인 공간에서의 표현의 자유는 최대한 폭넓게 보장되어야 한다: I think that freedom of expression in online spaces should be guaranteed as broadly as possible, while premised on the fact that it does not cause clear harm to others. This is because a society can healthily debate and develop only when diverse opinions can come and go freely. However, allowing speech that causes actual damage without limit, such as hate speech or the spread of false information, is close to abandonment under the guise of freedom. I think the criticism that the criteria by which platform companies delete content are arbitrary is also valid. Therefore, I think that freedom of expression and the prevention of harm can be established together only when clearly and transparently stating standards by law is a prerequisite. In that regulation becomes censorship if excessive and violence if neglected, this balance is an issue that must be continuously adjusted.
C1:나는 투표를 법적으로 의무화하는 것에 대체로 찬성하는 입장이다. 투: I am generally in favor of making voting legally mandatory. This is because if voter turnout is low, there is a risk that the voices of specific generations or classes will be overly reflected in policies. In fact, one cannot deny the fact that voter turnout in countries implementing mandatory voting is noticeably higher than in most countries. However, the counterargument that forcing unwanted voting infringes on individual freedom is also fully valid. Nevertheless, since I believe it is no exaggeration to say that the foundation of democracy lies in citizen participation, I think that compromising by allowing blank ballots can guarantee freedom and participation at the same time. Ultimately, I believe that combining it with institutional incentives that encourage participation rather than complete compulsion is a realistic alternative.
C1:나는 유전 질환을 예방할 목적의 배아 유전자 편집은 제한적으로 허용: I think that embryonic gene editing for the purpose of preventing genetic diseases may be allowed on a limited basis. This is because as genetic technology becomes more sophisticated, the possibility of blocking specific genetic diseases in advance is becoming a reality. Its significance is by no means small in that this technology can substantially reduce the suffering of future generations who would suffer from diseases. However, the possibility of being abused as so-called designer babies, selecting traits such as appearance or intelligence beyond the therapeutic purpose, cannot be excluded. To prevent these side effects, I believe international standards are needed to strictly limit the editable range to disease prevention. A cautious approach to finding a balance between the benefits of technology and ethical risks must come first.
C1:나는 무한한 경제 성장을 추구하는 방식은 이제 한계에 다다랐다고 생: I think the way of pursuing infinite economic growth has now reached its limit. The attitude of making growth the top priority even though resources are finite inevitably leads to environmental destruction. Therefore, I believe it is proper to transition to a sustainable society even if we endure a certain degree of slowdown in growth. Of course, the counterargument that a slowdown in growth can reduce jobs and make the lives of ordinary people difficult is also quite persuasive. However, I think that the price to pay if we neglect the climate crisis is much greater, even at the cost of short-term economic losses. Therefore, I think that de-growth does not mean poverty itself, but should be accepted as a process of re-establishing the very definition of growth.
C1:나는 청소년의 스마트폰 사용 시간을 법으로 제한하는 방안에 조건부로: I conditionally agree with the plan to legally limit the smartphone usage time of adolescents. While research results showing that excessive use leads to sleep deprivation and decreased concentration have already accumulated considerably, the reality is that it is difficult to guarantee effectiveness solely through parental autonomous guidance. Of course, the criticism that the state excessively intervenes in individual lives is also valid. Nevertheless, considering the impact on brain development and mental health during the growing period, I believe a minimum institutional device is necessary. However, a flexible approach, such as limiting nighttime usage rather than a uniform ban, would be more realistic. Ultimately, I think legal restrictions should be understood not as coercion, but as an auxiliary device to create healthy habits.
C1:나는 기후 위기 대응을 위해 원자력 발전을 당분간 확대할 필요가 있: I think it is necessary to expand nuclear power generation for the time being to respond to the climate crisis. While solar and wind power do not emit carbon, they have a limitation in that the volatility of power generation is still too large to be responsible for stable large-scale supply. On the other hand, nuclear power can supply stable power with a small site, making it an alternative that can quickly replace fossil fuels. Of course, fundamental problems such as radioactive waste disposal and accident risks can never be taken lightly. Therefore, even if nuclear power is expanded, safety standards and waste management systems must be strengthened together. Ultimately, I think utilizing nuclear power as a transitional means until renewable energy technology is sufficiently mature is a realistic choice.
C1:나는 주 4일 근무제를 전면적으로 법제화하는 것에는 아직 시기상조라: I am of the position that it is still premature to comprehensively legislate the four-day work week system. It is true that the results that productivity actually improved following some companies' pilot operations became a hot topic. However, it is difficult to see these results applied equally to companies of all industries and sizes. In particular, in small and medium-sized enterprises lacking human resources or industries where shift work is essential, a reduction in working days can directly lead to labor cost burdens and work gaps. Nevertheless, I also agree with the broad trend that we should move in the direction of raising labor productivity and quality of life together in the long run. Therefore, I think a method of phased expansion through pilot introduction by industry rather than a full mandatory enforcement is more desirable.
C1:나는 육류 소비에 세금을 부과하는 정책에 신중하게나마 찬성하는 입장: I am in favor, albeit cautiously, of a policy to tax meat consumption. This is because it cannot be denied that the livestock industry accounts for a significant portion of greenhouse gas emissions. If taxes induce consumers to choose alternative foods instead of meat, it ultimately contributes to reducing environmental burdens. However, it cannot be ignored that there is a risk that such taxes will increase the food cost burden of low-income families and act virtually like a regressive tax. Therefore, I believe that plans to reinvest the financial resources collected through taxes into alternative protein food subsidies or low-income support should be prepared together. Ultimately, this policy will be able to play its role when designed in a direction that helps consumer transition rather than simple punitive taxation.
C1:나는 소득 수준을 막론하고 모든 국민에게 기본적인 의료 서비스가 보: I think basic medical services should be guaranteed for all citizens regardless of income level. In a private insurance-centered system, people who cannot afford insurance premiums actually end up delaying even essential treatment. Facing this reality, there is no way not to recognize the necessity of the public medical system. Of course, the concern that expanding public insurance will increase tax burdens and lengthen waiting times is also well-founded. However, leaving fundamental rights such as life and health solely to market logic has too great a social risk. Therefore, I think it is desirable to leave private insurance as a supplementary means while guaranteeing at least basic access to medical care through the public system.
C1:나는 교도소 운영의 초점이 처벌에서 재사회화로 옮겨 가야 한다고 생: I think the focus of prison operation should shift from punishment to resocialization. This is because the purpose of punishment should not just be to isolate criminals, but to help them not commit crimes again when they return to society. There are many studies showing that equipping resocialization programs such as vocational training and psychological counseling substantively before strengthening punishment is more effective in lowering recidivism rates. Of course, the counterargument that treating violent criminals too leniently can undermine the sense of justice of victims and society cannot be ignored. Therefore, a detailed approach that applies different proportions of punishment and reformation depending on the severity of the crime is necessary. Ultimately, even to break the vicious cycle of recidivism that cannot be solved by punishment alone, the transition centered on reformation is inevitable.
C1:나는 대체 실험 방법이 아직 완전하지 않은 현재로서는 최소한의 동물: I think minimal animal testing is inevitable for now, while alternative testing methods are not yet complete. This is because it is true that there is a lack of other reliable methods to verify safety before applying it directly to humans. However, it must be premised on the clear verification of the necessity of the experiment, and unnecessary or duplicate experiments must be strictly limited. Its role was by no means small, to the extent that it is no exaggeration to say that a significant portion of new drug development today has gone through animal testing. Nevertheless, I believe that the ethical duty to minimize animal suffering must also be kept. Therefore, rather than completely banning animal testing, a direction that actively combines alternative technologies such as cell culture or computer simulation and gradually reduces its proportion is realistic.
C1:나는 채용 과정에 인공지능 알고리즘을 부분적으로 활용하는 것에는 찬: I am in favor of partially utilizing artificial intelligence algorithms in the hiring process, but against relying on them entirely. While artificial intelligence can review massive applications quickly and with consistent criteria, the risk of reproducing biases as they are if there are biases in past data used for learning cannot be excluded. In fact, cases of algorithms working to the advantage of specific genders or educational backgrounds have already been reported several times. Nevertheless, considering that human interviewers are also not free from unconscious prejudices, I believe there is no reason to unconditionally exclude artificial intelligence. Therefore, I think it is desirable that humans make the final judgment while algorithms are utilized only in auxiliary stages such as document review. I think this is an area where trusting and monitoring technology are needed at the same time.
C1:나는 회복 가능성이 없는 말기 환자에 한해 안락사를 제한적으로 합법: I am in favor of conditionally legalizing euthanasia limited to terminally ill patients without the possibility of recovery. This is because extending life in extreme pain cannot necessarily be seen as best for that person. One cannot help but acknowledge that the right to finish life with dignity also belongs to an individual's right to self-determination. However, this system must be premised on strict medical judgment and clear confirmation of the person's own intentions. Otherwise, side effects may arise where people are driven to choose unwanted deaths due to economic burdens or family pressure. Therefore, I think the legalization of euthanasia should be introduced cautiously only when strict procedures and multiple verification devices are equipped together.
C1:나는 사형 제도를 폐지하는 것이 바람직하다고 생각한다. 흉악 범죄에: I think it is desirable to abolish the death penalty. Punishment for heinous crimes should not just end with resolving social anger, but achieve the practical purpose of preventing recurrence, and looking at various research results, it is difficult to see the death penalty as having a greater crime deterrent effect than other punishments. Rather, the fact that cases of innocent people being executed due to misjudgment have been reported all over the world shows the fatal risk of this system. Of course, I fully understand that from the perspective of victims of heinous crimes and their bereaved families, the death penalty may feel like the only justice. Nevertheless, I believe we must be extremely cautious when the state executes an irreversible punishment. Therefore, I think a penal system that leaves room for reversal, such as life imprisonment without parole instead of the death penalty, is more rational.
C1:나는 공공장소에서의 안면 인식 기술 도입을 매우 제한적으로만 허용해: I think the introduction of facial recognition technology in public places should be allowed only very restrictively. As technology becomes more sophisticated, it is undeniable that its potential to be utilized for catching criminals or searching for missing persons has grown. However, at the same time, the risk that governments or corporations can easily accumulate individuals' daily movements has grown just as much. I think a society where the freedom to walk the streets anonymously practically disappears is likely to degenerate into a surveillance society. Therefore, I think its use should be allowed only in cases with clear purposes and legal grounds, such as criminal investigations, and expansion to routine mass surveillance must be prevented. An attitude that considers the impact on individual freedom as much as the convenience of technology is necessary.
C1:나는 현금 없는 사회로의 전환을 무리하게 서두르는 것에는 반대하는: I am against unreasonably rushing the transition to a cashless society. While digital payments make transactions convenient, the elderly or classes with low digital accessibility face a high risk of being alienated from basic economic activities. People without bank accounts or smartphones insisting on cash despite inconveniences have their own reasons, so to speak. Of course, it is also true that cash distribution is accompanied by side effects such as counterfeiting or tax evasion. Nevertheless, I think the right to choose payment methods should be left as a minimum social safety net. Therefore, a balanced policy that encourages digital payments but does not completely exclude cash use legally is needed.
C1:나는 긱 이코노미 노동자들에게도 최소한의 사회 보호 장치가 제공되어: I think minimum social protection devices should be provided to gig economy workers as well. Triggered by the spread of platform labor, the precarious plight faced by workers in this field has received great social attention. In many cases, they shoulder risks entirely individually without compensation for accidents or illness. Of course, from the company's point of view, they express reluctance to expand protection by putting forward that they must maintain flexible working patterns. However, I believe that flexible work and the creation of a minimum safety net are not values that are mutually exclusive. Therefore, I think basic protection devices such as industrial accident insurance or minimum income guarantees should be legally mandated.
C1:나는 일회용 플라스틱 사용을 단계적으로 전면 금지하는 것이 마땅하다: I think it is proper to phase out and completely ban single-use plastics. This is because the damage caused by plastic waste to marine ecosystems and human health has already reached a serious level. Considering the reality that the price of alternatives is still relatively expensive, concerns that the burden on small business owners may increase are fully understandable. However, the speed of environmental destruction is too fast to delay response for this reason.
