Standardized greetings and facial expression management required of call center agents or sales workers act as mechanisms regulating even the worker's inner self beyond simple service manuals. The implicit norm that calmness must be maintained despite unreasonable customer demands or verbal abuse places considerable burden on workers' mental health, and this often leads to emotional exhaustion and depression in the long term. In the past when social awareness of emotional labor was low, this burden was regarded only as an individual's share, but as related research accumulated, it is treated as a clear industrial accident area. The establishment of institutional devices such as emotional labor protection laws can be said to be the result of acknowledging that this problem is an area of social responsibility beyond the problem of individual patience. Unless respect for emotional labor settles within corporate culture, fundamental improvement cannot be expected solely through institutional protection, and practical changes also require changes in consumers' awareness. Ultimately, the institutionalization of emotional labor can be said to show the process where the growth of the service industry created new forms of labor and new risks simultaneously.
C2:온돌은 아궁이에서 발생한 열기를 방바닥 아래의 구들장으로 통과시켜: Ondol is a heating method unique to Korea that heats the entire indoor space by passing heat generated from a furnace through guudeuljang under the floor, and has deeply influenced Koreans' lifestyle habits overall for a long time. A heating method warming the floor naturally develops sitting-style life, so in the ondol cultural sphere, living patterns sitting and lying on the room floor rather than beds or high chairs settled as standards for a long time. The view looking at Western-style bed culture solely from the perspective of convenience is also pointed out as merely overlooking the physical and emotional utility that ondol possesses. The structure of the ondol space where the whole family sits gathered together on a warm floor naturally narrows the physical distance among family members, and this also influenced the formation of family-centered housing culture unique to Korea. Hot water circulation floor heating introduced in modern apartments merely inherits the principle of traditional ondol, but the heat source and construction method are completely different. The traditional living rhythm of preparing firewood and managing the furnace for winter heating naturally enabled people to internalize how to organize life according to seasonal changes. Even today, many foreigners express surprise at its uniqueness after experiencing Korea's floor heating method. Ultimately, ondol can be said to be a cultural device that has formed Koreans' physical habits, family culture, and spatial perception overall beyond a simple heating technology.
C2:능력주의는 얼핏 가장 공정한 원칙처럼 보이지만, 나는 그 공정함이: At a glance, meritocracy seems like the fairest principle, but I think that fairness is largely an illusion. I have no intention of denying the principle itself that people should be rewarded as much as they try. However, it keeps bothering me that the conditions even to try in the first place are already very different for each person. A child born into a rich family and a child not born into one seem to stand at the same starting line, but actually, they start the race from completely different points. Still, if we only look at the result, praise the winner's ability, and blame the loser's laziness, that is nothing more than sophisticated language that justifies inequality. The core of the problem is not that we should not reward effort, but that victory and defeat are already largely decided even before people start trying. Therefore, I believe that for meritocracy to function as true fairness, society must take responsibility for at least equality of the starting point, if not equality of outcome. I want to argue that my point is not to scrap meritocracy, but to fix its preconditions first so that it actually works as a principle rather than a myth.
C2:예술이 반드시 관객을 필요로 하는가라는 질문에 나는 그렇지 않다고: To the question of whether art necessarily needs an audience, I want to answer that it does not. Of course, I fully understand the thoughts of people who believe a work is only completed when it reaches someone. However, even for a picture that no one sees, I think the immersion and discovery the painter felt while drawing it are already a complete experience in themselves. Some might say that without a viewer, that creation is just a private scribble, but I think that judgment is too hasty. The act of creation is inherently an attempt to sort out one's inner self and understand the world anew, and the essence of art is already contained within that process itself. Of course, I cannot deny the point that art gets richer meaning when it is circulated and interpreted within society. Even so, I think the presence or absence of an audience should not be the sole criterion that determines the value of a work. Ultimately, I believe that the necessary condition for art is not communication, but sincere expression.
C2:아직 태어나지도 않은 미래 세대에게 우리가 도덕적 의무를 지닌다는: Although the claim that we have moral obligations to future generations who are not even born yet may sound abstract at first glance, I think it is by no means an empty phrase. Of course, the counterargument of how we can calculate the interests of non-existent beings right now also makes sense. Even considering the uncertainty that we cannot accurately predict their specific needs or desires right now, I believe the principle that we must at least hand down a livable global environment should not be shaken. No matter how much we save and use resources sparingly today, the ones who will directly enjoy those benefits will not be ourselves, but the next generation. Even so, if we do not make that effort now, the price they will have to bear later will be unimaginably large. I think that excluding their interests from the calculation altogether just because the existence of future generations is uncertain is close to an evasion of responsibility. Therefore, I argue that in policy decisions, the interests of future generations should be treated with equal weight to those of the present generation.
C2:문화 차용과 문화 교류를 명확히 구분하지 않고 모든 차용을 싸잡아: The attitude of condemning all borrowing by lumping it together without clearly distinguishing between cultural appropriation and cultural exchange is truly regrettable. Of course, we must admit that there actually are cases where people consume the symbols or traditions of a specific group without context and only take profits. However, if we demonize the contact itself where different cultures meet, human cultural history could not have been established in the first place. I think the attitude of bringing something is a more important criterion than the act of bringing a certain element itself. If we approach with a posture of acknowledging the origin, respecting its context, and trying to learn, that meeting can be used as an opportunity to enrich each other and lead to new creation. Conversely, if we just pluck and consume exotic elements without respect for the original creator, I think that is close to exploitation. Ultimately, I believe the core lies not in the dichotomy dividing whether it is appropriation or exchange, but in the practical attitude of respect and recognition.
C2:디지털 기록이 영구히 남는 시대로 말미암아 '잊힐 권리'에 대한 요: Due to the era where digital records remain permanently, the demand for the 'right to be forgotten' is growing increasingly, and I think this right holds considerable legitimacy. A situation where mistakes from youth or distorted information remain at the top of search results for a lifetime and continue to squeeze a person's life is definitely unfair. However, we cannot ignore the concern that if we recognize this right without limit, it will eventually turn into a means of erasing uncomfortable truths. If even information related to the public interest, especially records like past corruption by public officials, becomes the target of deletion requests, it will not be the right to be forgotten, but a tool for avoiding responsibility. Therefore, I believe this right must be delicately adjusted between individual dignity and the right to know. The criteria for deletion should be judged on a case-by-case basis, comprehensively considering the public interest, the passage of time, and the nature of the information. Ultimately, I conclude that the right to be forgotten is not an absolute right, but a relative right that must be constantly weighed against other rights.
C2:기술이 사회 변화의 유일한 동력이라는 기술 결정론에는 나는 동의하기: It is difficult for me to agree with technological determinism, which claims that technology is the sole driving force of social change. Although it is undeniable that our lifestyles change greatly every time a new technology appears, it is hard to see technology itself as entirely determining the direction and speed of that change. There are plenty of cases where the same technology produces completely different results depending on the institutions and values of the society that introduces it. I think describing human history as if it were reduced to the automatic product of technological development stages is excessively simple. Rather, we must not forget that choosing what technology to develop and how to regulate it is ultimately a human political decision. Of course, I also admit that technology has strong inertia in the sense that it is difficult to roll back a technology once it has spread widely. Even so, I believe that humans are not completely helpless beings in front of that inertia. Ultimately, the relationship between technology and humans should be understood not as unilateral domination, but as constant interaction.
C2:번역은 반역이라는 오래된 격언에 나는 절반만 동의한다. 원문의 미묘: I only half agree with the old adage that translation is betrayal. I admit that it is fundamentally impossible to perfectly transfer the subtle nuances and rhythm of an original text into another language. However, I think it is excessive to conclude that translation is a betrayal of the original text. Rather than not translating at all for the reason that it cannot be translated perfectly, opening that world to readers of another language, even if somewhat imperfectly, is a much more valuable thing. As a translator reads the original text over and over and searches for the best expression, they realize that the process itself has somehow become another creation. I believe that even if the form of the original text is lost, the spirit contained within it can live again in the new language. Therefore, I think it is more accurate to understand translation not as betrayal, but as migration to another language, or re-creation. The fact that there is a loss does not mean it is a betrayal.
C2:넛지, 즉 사람들의 선택을 부드럽게 유도하는 정책 설계에 대해 나는: Regarding nudges, which are policy designs that gently guide people's choices, I am in conditional agreement. Nudges must basically be designed on the premise that individuals can still make other choices in order to gain legitimacy. For example, the degree of displaying healthy food so that it catches the eye easily is a method that can induce good results without infringing on the freedom of choice. However, if that design intent and method are carried out while completely hidden, I think that is nothing other than manipulation, not persuasion. If people cannot even know the fact that they are being guided, the value of autonomy becomes hollowed out. Therefore, I believe the institutions designing nudges should bear the obligation to transparently disclose their purpose and method. Also, they must clearly leave open a pathway to return to the original choice at any time. Ultimately, the legitimacy of a nudge depends on whether it completely replaces freedom or still respects and assists freedom.
C2:개인과 공동체의 기억은 흔히 부정확하다는 이유로 역사학의 엄밀함에: The memories of individuals and communities are easily pushed aside by the rigor of history on the grounds that they are often inaccurate, but I think memory is a precious material that preserves the texture of emotion that history easily misses. Of course, memory has clear limitations as historical material in that it gets distorted and selectively edited as time passes. However, in order to revive voices that are not left in official records, it is necessary to collect testimonies and oral histories even at the risk of distortion. If history builds the skeleton of an event, memory plays the role of putting living emotions onto that skeleton. I think it is correct to understand the two as complementary relations rather than pitting them against each other. Of course, historical facts should not be judged by memory alone, and they must go through cross-verification with other materials. Nevertheless, I believe that the work of reclaiming memories pushed out of official historical narratives is absolutely necessary for a complete understanding of the past.
C2:아름다움의 기준이 전적으로 문화에 따라 다르다는 주장에 나는 대체로: I mostly agree with the claim that the criteria of beauty depend entirely on culture, but not completely. We cannot ignore research showing that regardless of era and region, a preference for symmetrical faces or healthy-looking bodies appears to some extent in common. However, what kind of body shape, skin color, and expression are specifically considered ideal varies surprisingly from society to society. There is hardly any phenomenon more concerning than the recent trend where global mass media spread a specific region's beauty standards like a norm. This is effectively narrowing the diverse senses of beauty down into a single commercial standard. As a result, many people consider their own unique traits like flaws and suffer unnecessary pain. Therefore, I think we should examine more critically whose interests the standards are formed and circulated for, rather than the universality of aesthetic standards.
C2:오늘날 사생활 보호는 어느새 특정 계층만이 온전히 누릴 수 있는 사: I deeply sympathize with the fact that today, privacy is gradually turning into a luxury item that only a specific class can fully enjoy. The reality where we have to use paid services and equip ourselves with expensive security devices to avoid data tracking has now gone beyond the problem of individual choice and become a problem of structural inequality. The principle that everyone, regardless of income level, should be guaranteed a minimum level of privacy is increasingly degrading into an empty slogan. Low-income groups are placed in a position where they have to hand over much more of their own data as the price for free services. On the other hand, people with means purchase privacy as a product and are relatively free from that risk. If we leave this gap neglected as it is, privacy will solidify not as a human right, but as a privilege traded in the market. Therefore, I believe that policies defining minimum digital privacy as a fundamental right and institutionally guaranteeing it are urgent.
C2:모든 행동이 이전 원인에 의해 결정되어 있다는 결정론이 사실이라 할: Even if determinism, which states that all actions are determined by prior causes, is true, I think we should not completely abandon the concept of moral responsibility. Of course, the development of neuroscience is increasingly and persuasively showing that human choices may not be the product of pure free will, but the result of the brain's physical actions. Whenever I encounter this debate, I tend to feel a confusion reminiscent of the fierce debates taking place in a philosophy class. However, even if determinism is metaphysically true, society's practice of holding individuals responsible for their actions still has an important practical function. If we do not hold people responsible, the social devices of punishment, education, and compensation themselves will lose meaning. Therefore, I argue that even if there is no metaphysical free will, the concept of responsibility on a social and practical level must be maintained. Ultimately, I believe we can construct a responsible society without waiting for the answers of metaphysics.
C2:정의가 실현되려면 반드시 용서가 뒤따라야 하는가라는 질문에 나는 그: To the question of whether forgiveness must necessarily follow for justice to be realized, I want to answer that it does not. I think the core of justice does not lie in guiding the victim's emotions in a specific direction, but in fairly holding people accountable in proportion to their wrongdoing. Forgiveness is something that should well up from inside the individual victim, and it is not a nature that society can force or expect. The narrative that victims must automatically grant forgiveness in exchange for the perpetrator's reflection instead places another burden on the victim. Of course, I respect the point that forgiveness can be a path to healing for the parties involved. However, we cannot blame a person for hindering justice just because they do not forgive. Ultimately, I think justice must be dealt with on a separate axis from forgiveness, and the moment the two are mixed, there is a risk that the true determination of responsibility will become blurred.
C2:기본소득이 노동 의욕을 근본적으로 무너뜨릴 것이라는 우려에 나는 전: I do not entirely agree with the concern that a basic income will fundamentally destroy the will to work. Of course, the worry that no one will work if a minimum livelihood is guaranteed looks intuitively plausible. However, we must not overlook the fact that regardless of income level, what people want to get from labor is not just living expenses, but a sense of achievement and social belonging. In an era where jobs themselves are shrinking due to automation, demanding that people prove their dignity only through labor is nothing other than an unrealistic demand. Rather, when there is a minimum safety net, people can afford to take risks, try starting a business, or receive retraining. Of course, the issue of securing financial resources and the side effects it will bring to the labor market must be reviewed carefully. Nevertheless, I believe that a basic income can be designed as a device that expands labor options rather than replacing labor.
C2:혐오 표현을 법으로 규제해야 하는가에 대해 나는 제한적으로 찬성하는: Regarding whether hate speech should be regulated by law, I am in conditional agreement. I think it is wrong to leave even the organized incitement of violence toward a specific group unchecked under the pretext of the principle of freedom of expression. Actually, hate speech practically threatens the safety and dignity of minorities, and the damage is by no means abstract. However, I think we should also guard against setting the scope of regulation too widely at the risk of shrinking freedom of expression. When the boundary of what is hate and what is legitimate criticism becomes ambiguous, the side with power can abuse that ambiguity as a tool to suppress statements unfavorable to them. Therefore, regulation must be limited to a narrow scope with clear standards, such as when it directly incites violence or targets a specific group. Ultimately, I think the balance between freedom and safety is not a matter of principles, but a matter of delicate design.
C2:지나간 시절을 그리워하는 향수치고 완전히 순수한 감정은 드물다고 나: I think that among nostalgias yearning for past days, completely pure emotions are rare. People usually erase the hard parts, selectively leave only the good memories, and paint the past more beautifully than it actually was. This phenomenon, which commonly appears regardless of generation, may itself be a natural psychological defense mechanism. However, the story changes when this nostalgia goes beyond individual recollection and is mobilized as political language. Narratives that unconditionally paint a specific period of the past as an ideal era often conveniently erase the inequality and violence of those days. If we design policies relying on such distorted nostalgia, there is a big risk that it will lead to a vain attempt to return to a past that never existed instead of facing current problems. Therefore, I think nostalgia should be allowed in the realm of personal comfort, but always guarded against as a basis for public judgment.
C2:유전자를 조작해 질병을 막는 기술과 아이를 더 뛰어나게 만들려는 기: I think the technology of manipulating genes to prevent disease and the technology of making children more talented are completely different issues. Editing to prevent fatal genetic disorders can be seen as a legitimate intervention akin to medical treatment. However, editing to enhance traits such as intelligence or appearance gives rise to problems on a completely different dimension. If wealthy parents can buy genetic advantages for their children in exchange for huge costs, it will result in solidifying existing inequalities even down to the biological level. In a situation where socioeconomic gaps are already reproducing across multiple generations, if gene editing is even added, that gap might widen to an irreversible level. Therefore, I believe gene editing for therapeutic purposes should be allowed cautiously, while editing aimed at enhancement should be strongly regulated. The fact that technology is possible does not become an argument that it must be allowed.
C2:사형 제도가 정의를 실현하는 최종적인 수단이라는 주장에 나는 동의하: I do not agree with the claim that the death penalty is the ultimate means of realizing justice. No matter how careful a trial is, as long as humans conduct it, the possibility of misjudgment does not disappear. Cases where innocence was later revealed after the death penalty was carried out have painfully proven the danger of this system. If the practical function of the death penalty is for the state to execute anger over violent crime on behalf of citizens, I think it is nothing more than revenge carried out by the state rather than the realization of justice. Moreover, statistical evidence that the death penalty actually deters violent crime is not clear. If society can be sufficiently protected from danger through alternatives like life imprisonment, the reasons to stubbornly maintain an irreversible punishment decrease. Therefore, I argue that the death penalty system should be phased out and we should move toward a punishment system without the risk of misjudgment.
C2:국경이라는 것이 도덕적으로 완전히 정당화될 수 있는가라는 질문에 나: To the question of whether borders can be morally completely justified, I end up answering with complicated feelings. Even if a community called a state sets a certain degree of boundaries to operate resources and systems, I think those boundaries should not become walls blocking people's lives and dignity. However, the reality today is full of contradictions: while capital and goods cross borders freely, actual people are blocked by much stricter barriers. The fact that someone's life opportunities are drastically split merely by the accidental condition of where they were born is difficult to justify morally. Of course, I also acknowledge that the argument to completely eliminate borders can produce various side effects in reality. Then, I believe that at least for refugees or people moving for survival, we must apply much more lenient principles than now. My thought is that while I do not deny the existence of borders itself, they must not function merely as tools to protect privileges.
C2:동물이 인간과 완전히 동등한 권리를 지녀야 하는가에 대해서는 신중한: Regarding whether animals should have completely equal rights with humans, I hold a cautious stance, but I am convinced that just the fact that animals can feel pain means they should receive considerable moral consideration. Due to the development of neuroscience, it is becoming increasingly clear that many animals experience pain and fear in ways similar to humans. There are clear differences in cognitive abilities between humans and animals, and that difference cannot be the basis for ignoring animals' pain. In particular, I think the pain suffered by animals mass-raised through factory farming methods is difficult to justify by any ethical standard. Applying the exact same list of rights to humans and animals may be unrealistic, but the principle that unnecessary pain must be minimized must be kept without exception. Therefore, I want to argue that rather than granting animals the exact same legal status as humans, the effort to reduce pain belongs in the realm of moral obligation.
C2:인공지능이 만든 그림을 예술로 인정할 수 있느냐는 질문에 나는 완전: To the question of whether art made by artificial intelligence can be recognized as art, I do not want to give a complete affirmation or a complete negation. If we grant the qualification of art simply based on the fact that the result is visually beautiful, rather than denying that it is art, it might be a more honest attitude to recognize it as a new category. However, as human artists repeat failures endlessly and try to shape their emotions and experiences, it is difficult to deny that that process itself occupies a large part of the work's meaning. Artificial intelligence can learn vast amounts of data and produce plausible results, but it is hard to view personal agony or concrete life contexts as contained behind that. Therefore, I think it is more reasonable to classify results made by artificial intelligence as a separate creation rather than comparing them on the same tier as human art. Both can be objects of appreciation in their own ways, but I believe the grounds for their value are different.
C2:자유시장이 환경 지속가능성과 양립할 수 있는가에 대해 나는 조건부로: To the question of whether the free market can be compatible with environmental sustainability, I want to answer yes, conditionally. For the market to harmonize with sustainability, it must be premised on the fact that the costs of environmental destruction are accurately reflected in prices. However, the market in reality operates while hardly reflecting the costs of external effects like air pollution or resource depletion. As a result, companies operate within a distorted incentive structure where ways of destroying the environment are actually cheaper choices. Carbon pricing or taxation on pollution-causing industries are realistic means that can correct the market's signaling system in a sustainable direction, in my opinion. There is no need to deny the market itself, but leaving environmental problems to an unregulated market is close to a dangerous gamble. Ultimately, I believe whether the market and sustainability are compatible depends on what rules are designed inside the market.
C2:공공의 안전을 위해서라면 광범위한 감시가 정당화될 수 있다는 주장에: I am skeptical about the claim that extensive surveillance can be justified if it is for public safety. Surveillance conducted by treating most citizens as potential suspects is actually mortgaging the freedom of the majority to prevent the threats of a minority. As surveillance technology becomes more sophisticated, its targets tend to go beyond originally intended terrorism or serious crimes to include the everyday actions of ordinary citizens. It is also concerning that historically, it is very rare for a government to reduce surveillance powers once it secures them. Of course, in situations where a specific threat is concretely confirmed, surveillance that is limited and under judicial control may be inevitable. However, the moment that exception hardens into an everyday principle, trust between citizens and the state is damaged to a level that is difficult to restore. Therefore, I think strict judicial controls on the scope and period of surveillance must definitely be prepared together.
C2:오래된 전통이라 할지라도 그것이 무조건 보존되어야 한다고는 생각하지: Even if it is an old tradition, I do not think it should be preserved unconditionally. I believe the value of a tradition lies not in how old it is, but in whether it practically enriches people's lives even at this very moment. Some customs still function as precious assets that protect a community's identity and bonds, while other customs remain merely as tools to justify outdated discrimination and oppression. I think the attitude of exempting a specific practice from criticism simply on the fact that it is old is dangerous. Of course, if we hastily discard traditions, there is also the risk that meanings and a sense of belonging shared by the community will be damaged. Therefore, instead of the dichotomy of unconditionally keeping or unconditionally discarding traditions, I think we must constantly check who benefits and who is harmed by them today. Ultimately, the qualification of a tradition to survive depends not on age, but on usefulness and justice.
C2:내부 고발이 조직에 대한 배신인가, 아니면 정당한 용기인가라는 질문: To the question of whether whistleblowing is a betrayal of the organization or justified courage, I think it is closer to the latter. We have already witnessed through various events that any organization has an incentive to hide internal problems rather than reveal them itself. Considering that whistleblowers are often criticized for abandoning loyalty to the organization, I think remaining silent while knowing facts that clearly harm the public interest is a greater betrayal. Without people who took the risk of personal disadvantage and retaliation to reveal the truth, numerous irregularities and dangers would have been concealed until now. Of course, not all exposures stem from public interest motives, and cases mixed with personal grudge or exaggerated claims certainly exist. Therefore, the legitimacy of an exposure must be judged based on how concrete its content is and how directly connected it is to the public interest. Nevertheless, I believe that systems protecting whistleblowers in principle should be prepared much more thickly.
C2:애국심과 세계시민주의가 서로 양립할 수 없다는 통념에 나는 동의하지: I do not agree with the common notion that patriotism and cosmopolitanism cannot be compatible with each other. I think we can use the mindset of looking at our belonging community with affectionate eyes as an opportunity to instead broaden the scope of understanding other communities. The problem is not patriotism itself, but when it is distorted into a basis for excluding other countries and other people. Exclusive patriotism is not true patriotism, but merely packages defensive psychology created by fear under the name of patriotism. On the other hand, affection for the land, language, and history where one grew up can coexist just fine with the attitude of respecting other cultures. In fact, research shows that people who have a healthy sense of belonging to their own community tend to naturally respect the sense of belonging of others as well. Therefore, rather than demanding that people throw away patriotism, I want to argue that we should use it as a starting point for expanded solidarity rather than exclusiveness.
C2:부의 불평등이 그 자체로 부당한가라는 질문에 나는 정도와 원인에 따: To the question of whether wealth inequality is unfair in itself, I think we must answer differently depending on the degree and cause. I do not think there is any need to negate even the generation of a certain degree of disparity as a reward for effort and innovation. However, the problem is the fact that a large part of today's extreme wealth disparities cannot be explained by differences in ability, but by structures of inheritance and rent-seeking—meaning parents' wealth is directly converted into children's wealth. If this structure repeats across generations, society solidifies into a state practically no different from a caste system. In this situation, narratives explaining inequality purely as a lack of individual effort distort reality. Therefore, while respecting rewards for legitimate contributions, I think policy interventions such as progressive taxation and strengthening inheritance tax are necessary for inequalities caused by inherited privilege and rent-seeking. Ultimately, the core is not the presence of inequality, but whether that inequality originated from a fair process.
C2:소셜 미디어가 공적 담론의 질을 근본적으로 훼손했다는 진단에 나는: I largely agree with the diagnosis that social media has fundamentally damaged the quality of public discourse. The structure where algorithms preferentially expose stimulating and extreme content to increase engagement and retention time is nothing other than a device that encourages agitation over deliberation. Of course, we cannot ignore the aspect that social media gave a voice to people who previously had no channel to speak. However, the reality where unverified, stimulating information spreads indiscriminately under the pretext of freedom of expression is actually making the public sphere more vulnerable. I also want to point out that the platform structure itself, which induces short and immediate reactions, makes in-depth discussions on complex issues difficult. Therefore, I think the root of the problem lies not only in the attitudes of individual users, but in the design and profit structure of the platforms. Ultimately, to restore public discourse, efforts to redesign the way algorithms work must be made together.
C2:역사적 잘못에 대한 국가의 사과나 배상이 과연 의미가 있는가에 대해: Regarding whether a state's apology or compensation for historical wrongs is actually meaningful, I give a conditional affirmation. Official apologies made despite political burdens and backlash clearly have value in that they provide a minimum level of recognition to victims and their descendants. However, formal apologies without substantive institutional improvements following them easily end up as empty gestures. Apologies made only with words without compensation run the risk of being consumed as an alibi that past wrongs have been settled. For true reconciliation, substantive compensation for damages must be prepared along with an apology, as well as institutional devices to ensure the same wrong is not repeated. Of course, debates surrounding who should take responsibility today and how much for things from decades or hundreds of years ago are still complicated. Nevertheless, I believe that starting the process, even if imperfectly, is closer to justice than avoiding apologies and compensation.
C2:집중력이나 기억력을 높여 주는 인지 향상 약물의 사용을 둘러싼 논쟁: In the debate surrounding the use of cognitive enhancement drugs that boost concentration or memory, I think the issue of fairness is the most important. Regardless of whether situations are competitive like exams or admissions, accessibility to these drugs is by no means equal. People with more economic means can obtain these drugs easily, and the result reflects differences in resources rather than differences in skill. There were also reports that the reality of drug abuse unfolding in some college neighborhoods is heading toward aspects reminiscent of an arms race. Of course, the logic that individuals are free to do whatever they want with their bodies also makes sense. However, if that freedom acts as pressure that effectively forces other people to make the same choice, it can no longer be viewed simply as pure individual freedom. Therefore, I think the use of these drugs must be strictly regulated, at least in contexts where official evaluations are made.
C2:불치병으로 극심한 고통을 겪는 환자가 스스로 삶을 마감할 권리를 요: When patients suffering extreme pain from incurable diseases request the right to end their lives themselves, I think we should respect that request. Life is precious, but we cannot always view it as right to forcibly extend life at the cost of unbearable pain under the pretext of that preciousness. People facing death usually know their own bodies and pain more accurately than anyone else. Of course, we must cautiously guard against the risk that the assisted dying system will be abused, especially acting as subtle pressure on society's vulnerable. However, I believe that risk should be accepted not as grounds to ban the system altogether, but as a reason to prepare strict procedures and repeated verification devices. It is generally confirmed that if we go through repeated confirmation of intentions based on sufficient information and reviews by independent medical staff, risks can be managed to a large extent. Therefore, I believe that legalizing assisted dying under strict conditions is the path to respecting individual autonomy.
C2:언론이 완전히 객관적인 진실을 전달할 수 있다는 믿음은 순진한 이상: I think the belief that journalism can deliver completely objective truth is nothing more than a naive ideal. From the moment of choosing which event to report, down to the moment of picking which words to use, a reporter's perspective is bound to intervene in some way or another. However, even if perfect objectivity is impossible, I think the very principle of fact-checking and fair reporting does not become meaningless. The attitude of justifying mixing facts and opinions on the grounds that objectivity is impossible is a dangerous leap in logic. Rather, when acknowledging that complete objectivity is impossible, journalism can more faithfully make efforts to transparently reveal its perspective and include diverse viewpoints in a balanced way. Therefore, I think what should be demanded of journalism is not impossible pure objectivity, but transparency and sincere verification. If we cannot distinguish between these two, only cynicism toward journalism will grow.
C2:세계화가 문화적 정체성을 완전히 지워 버릴 것이라는 우려는 어떤 면: The concern that globalization will completely erase cultural identity is exaggerated in some ways, but in other ways, it is an extremely desperate reality. The situation where minority languages and local traditions are rapidly disappearing worldwide definitely has aspects accelerated by globalization. As giant platforms and pop culture flood the global market with content from a few specific cultural spheres, smaller cultural spheres' languages and stories are losing ground to stand on. But at the same time, globalization also becomes a creative field where different cultures meet and create new hybrid cultures. It is worth remembering that completely isolated, pure cultures have rarely even existed historically. Therefore, I think we should not view globalization only as cultural homogenization, but policies that consciously protect vulnerable languages and traditions must be carried out alongside that flow. The survival of culture is not guaranteed by itself, and social efforts must back it up.
C2:행복을 공공 정책의 명시적인 목표로 삼아야 하는가에 대해 나는 조심: Regarding whether happiness should be made an explicit goal of public policy, I am cautious but positive. Various studies have already shown that economic indicators like gross domestic product alone cannot fully capture the quality of life, and we frequently witness cases where citizens' lives actually get harder even as growth indicators rise. Rather than chasing only growth while completely ignoring happiness, I think it is much more rational to measure citizens' actual life satisfaction together and reflect it in policies. However, if we convert the concept of happiness into overly simple survey scores and make the figures themselves the goal, there is a risk that distortions will occur where we miss the essence. This is because if policymakers become immersed only in raising scores, people's actual living conditions can be pushed to the back burner. Therefore, I think happiness indices should not be the sole standard replacing economic indicators, but should be referenced in a balanced way as one of several indicators. Ultimately, what is important is not the index itself, but the actual changes in life pointed to by that index.
C2:알고리즘 추천 시스템이 우리의 자율성을 은밀히 잠식하고 있다는 주장: I largely sympathize with the claim that algorithmic recommendation systems are stealthily eroding our autonomy. These systems generally seem designed on the premise that users precisely know what they want themselves, but in reality, they often reconstruct users' tastes themselves in repeatedly biased directions. If you mindlessly follow content recommended every day, before you know it, the boundary between what you originally liked and what the algorithm made you like becomes blurred. Of course, we must also acknowledge that algorithms provide practical help in filtering out useful choices amid vast amounts of information. However, if that convenience is given at the price of stealthily narrowing the user's range of choices, it is hard to view it as true help. Therefore, I think we must guarantee much broader rights for users to understand and adjust the operating principles of recommendation systems. The balance between convenience and autonomy is not kept by itself, and can only be maintained through intentional design and regulation.
C2:고전이라 불리는 작품들이 시대를 초월해 영원히 그 지위를 지켜야 하: Regarding whether works called classics should transcend time and keep their status forever, I have a reserved stance. I think that works surviving for a long time touch deep layers of human experience, so their vitality is proof of a value that cannot be ignored. However, it is also an undeniable fact that the process itself of a work being designated as a classic has reflected the tastes and power of a specific era and specific class. The fact that works by female writers or non-Western writers have been systematically excluded from classic lists for a long time ultimately shows that those lists were not pure reflections of objective excellence, but products of a specific perspective. Therefore, I want to argue that rather than unconditionally negating existing classics, we must constantly reexamine and expand those lists. Values transcending time and prejudices of a specific era are often mixed inside the same text. True respect comes not from making lists sacred, but from continuing to question them, I believe.
C2:수치심이 사회적 통제의 도구로 사용되는 것에 대해 나는 이중적인 태: I have a dual attitude toward shame being used as a tool of social control. A certain degree of social criticism following a person who committed an obvious wrong can be a legitimate way to hold them accountable, but we frequently witness cases where that criticism crosses proper lines and spreads to a level destroying a person's entire life. Especially in online spaces, it is common for one minor mistake to instantly spread into unmanageable public shaming. In the sense that the intensity of punishment can be infinitely amplified regardless of the weight of the wrong, I think this kind of shame functions closer to entertainment than justice. Of course, even if shame is effective as a means to publicize the corruption of those with power, it does not justify indiscriminate attacks toward anonymous individuals. Therefore, rather than completely negating shame, I think we ourselves must exercise restraint so that it operates in a way guaranteeing proportionality and recoverability.
C2:온라인 익명성이 도덕적 책임감을 근본적으로 무너뜨린다는 주장에 나는: I only partially agree with the claim that online anonymity fundamentally destroys moral responsibility. I think the core of the problem lies not in the format of anonymity itself, but in the structure where no matter what behavior is done behind anonymity, no practical consequences follow. Psychological research backing up the observation that people become more irresponsible than usual when they cannot see the results of their actions with their own eyes also supports this. However, at the same time, anonymity provides a space where whistleblowers or minorities vulnerable to power can safely voice their thoughts. Therefore, rather than eliminating anonymity itself, I think the more fundamental solution is for platforms to have practical reporting and sanction systems that can prevent abuse. Whether anonymous or real-name, what ultimately makes people feel responsible are the possibility of punishment and community norms. Therefore, rather than simplifying anonymity as the cause of moral corruption, I argue that we should pay attention to the real cause: the absence of systems holding people accountable.
C2:조상이 저지른 잘못에 대해 오늘날의 후손이 죄책감을 느껴야 하는가라: To the question of whether today's descendants should feel guilt for wrongs committed by their ancestors, I want to answer with careful distinction. Even considering that direct moral guilt cannot be blamed for things that happened before individuals were even born, the story changes if the results of those wrongs structurally continue to this day. The emotion of guilt cannot be forced upon individual descendants, but I think the current generation must shoulder the responsibility together to fix inequalities caused by past injustices. Using these discussions as an opportunity, we can learn more clearly how to distinguish between guilt and responsibility. It is a demand to dismantle the unfair structures left behind by those sins together now, not for descendants to shoulder ancestors' sins. By distinguishing this way, I believe we can lead discussions toward constructive responsibility instead of defensive guilt. Ultimately, what is important is not forcing emotions, but practice in creating a just structure.
C2:현대 사회에서 흔히 이야기되는 '진정한 자아'라는 개념이 실제로 성: I am skeptical about whether the concept of the 'true self,' which is commonly talked about in modern society, is actually establishable. Advice to find a pure self completely unaffected by outside influences is effectively telling people to chase an illusion that does not even exist. Our tastes, beliefs, and even desires are the result of piled-up layers of the environment where we were born, people we met, and books we read. A perspective viewing authenticity as reducing down to a pure essence with social influences completely removed is difficult to establish in the first place. That does not mean I want to say the concept of authenticity itself is meaningless. Rather, I think it is more valid to redefine authenticity not as freedom from influence, but as consistency between the values one accepted and actual behavior. Ultimately, a true life is not a life without any influences, but a life living consistently with influences chosen through self-reflection, I believe.
A2:미안해요, 토요일에는 일이 있기 때문에 못 가요. 대신 다음 주에는: I'm sorry, but because I have things to do on Saturday, I can't go. Instead, I'll have time next week. Let's go together then!
A2:네, 열 시면 괜찮아요. 회의 자료가 필요하면 오늘 저녁에 보내 드: Yes, ten o'clock is fine. If you need the meeting materials, I'll send them this evening. See you tomorrow!
A2:정말 감사해요! 저는 일곱 시쯤 집에 도착해요. 그때 찾으러 갈게요: Thank you so much! I arrive home around seven o'clock. I'll go pick it up then.
A2:안녕하세요, 내일 두 시에는 회의에 가야 해요. 혹시 네 시로 바꿀: Hello, I have to go to a meeting at two o'clock tomorrow. Is it possible to change it to four o'clock? I'll wait for your reply.
A2:알려 주셔서 감사해요. 오전에는 출근해야 하지만 오후에는 집에 있어: Thank you for letting me know. I have to go to work in the morning, but I'm at home in the afternoon. Can you come in the afternoon?
I like pork belly the most. I haven't tried soft tofu stew yet. Let's go eat it together next time!
A2:감사합니다! 저는 금요일 저녁 여섯 시쯤 갈 수 있어요. 그 시간에: Thank you! I can go around six o'clock on Friday evening. Is the store open at that time?
A2:네, 지난주에 가 봤어요. 커피는 좋았지만 케이크는 아직 안 먹어: Yes, I went there last week. The coffee was good, but I haven't tried the cake yet. Shall we try going together this weekend?
A2:좋아요! 오늘은 날씨가 추워서 국밥을 먹는 게 더 좋아요. 열두 시: Sounds good! The weather is cold today, so eating gukbap is better. Let's meet in the lobby at twelve o'clock.
A2:저는 팔월에 부산에 가려고 해요. 바다에서 며칠 쉬려고 해요. 같이: I'm planning to go to Busan in August. I'm planning to rest for a few days at the sea. It would be really great if we went together!
A2:네, 제 차예요. 어제 늦게 와서 자리를 잘못 봤어요. 정말 죄송해: Yes, it's my car. I came late yesterday, so I misread the spot. I'm really sorry, I won't do it again.
Of course! Is it okay if we go at nine o'clock? I'll bring my car too.
A2:알려 주셔서 감사해요. 목요일 저녁 수업으로 바꿀까요? 그날 자리가: Thank you for letting me know. Shall we change to the Thursday evening class? Please let me know if there are spots on that day.
A2:저는 요즘 '나의 아저씨'를 보고 있어요. 조금 슬프지만 정말 잘: I've been watching 'My Mister' these days. It's a bit sad, but I think it's really well made. Try watching it over the weekend!
A2:먼저 프린터를 껐다가 다시 켜 보세요. 그래도 안 되면 2층 프린터: First, try turning the printer off and on again. If it still doesn't work, try using the 2nd floor printer. I'll contact the management team in the afternoon.
A2:네, 잘 보냈어요. 토요일에 청소를 하고 나서 친구랑 한강에 갔어요: Yes, I spent it well. After cleaning on Saturday, I went to the Han River with a friend. On Sunday, I also got plenty of rest.
A2:안내 감사합니다. 자기 전에 먹어도 괜찮아요? 그리고 커피를 마시기: Thank you for the information. Is it okay even if I take it before going to sleep? And am I not supposed to take the medicine before drinking coffee?
